title: Phase 5d: propagate user_action outcome back to client (acks, errors, visible UI feedback)
description:
Phase 5d: propagate user_action outcome back to the client and surface it in the UI.

Today the mobile client emits a user_action WS frame and considers the local lifecycle complete the moment ChannelTransport returns "Sent". Verified 2026-05-17 19:25 EDT on Pixel 9 Pro PID 15524: A2UI: submitA2uiAction ... result=Sent is the last log line for the action. The client has no information about what happened on the server side - whether the action was matched to a pending approval (uo5.8 / uo5.12), routed as conversational input (uo5.13, not yet landed), recorded as a no-op, or errored.

From the user's perspective the rendered surface stays exactly the same after the tap:

- The Button does not visually transition to a "processed" state.
- The surface is not dismissed.
- No spinner indicates "agent is thinking about your action."
- No error chip surfaces when the action could not be processed (e.g. no correlation found, dispatcher gate rejected, server-side serialization failure).
- The whole interaction is silently consumed.

This makes A2UI surfaces feel broken even when they actually work, and feel identically broken when they actually do break. The user has no signal to discriminate.

Desired behavior:

The server SHOULD emit a user_action_outcome (or equivalent) WS frame back to the client per inbound user_action, containing:

- frameId (correlation back to the originating user_action frame's id)
- outcome enum: matched_approval | injected_as_input | recorded_only | rejected | error
- detail (optional): error message, agent turn id if injected_as_input, approval scope decision if matched_approval, etc.
- timestamp

The client SHOULD then react visually to the outcome:

- matched_approval: surface dismisses or transitions to a "decision recorded" state with the chosen scope visible briefly.
- injected_as_input: surface shows a brief "sent" indicator and waits for the agent's next turn to land in the chat.
- recorded_only: surface shows a subtle "recorded" caption (low-key - this is the "you tapped a thing that didn't do anything visible" case).
- rejected: surface shows an error chip with the reason and stays interactive for retry.
- error: same as rejected but with a generic error message.

The exact visual treatment is up to mobile design; the contract is just that the outcome frame must arrive and the client must do SOMETHING visible with it.

Why this matters:

- Without an ack contract, every A2UI surface is a Schrödinger's tap. Users will lose trust in the feature whether or not the back-end is doing the right thing.
- This is also a hard prerequisite for any future work that involves multi-step flows (e.g. ToolApprovalCard where the agent's next turn explains what happened, or wizard-style surfaces where the next step depends on the action result).
- Pairs naturally with uo5.13: once non-approval actions are injected, the outcome ack would say "injected, expect agent response," giving the client a clear state to display while waiting.

Surfaces likely touched:

- admin-shim/lib/mobile-channel-host.ts handleUserAction - construct and emit a user_action_outcome frame on every return path.
- admin-shim/docs/MOBILE_WS_PROTOCOL.md - document the new frame type.
- Mobile renderer (filed as a sibling bead in letta-mobile when this lands here) - react to the outcome with visible UI state.

Non-goals:

- Detailed retry logic on the client (separate concern; the ack just needs to surface failure visibly).
- Rich animations or motion design (out of scope - just baseline visible feedback).
- Persistence of action outcomes across reload (separate, deferred).

Rollback signal:

If the outcome frame becomes noisy and clutters the chat (e.g. every approval ack emits a visible system message that piles up), revert and make the outcome frame ephemeral - it should drive UI state transitions but not become long-lived chat history unless the agent explicitly logs it.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Server emits a user_action_outcome WS frame for every inbound user_action, correlated by frameId, carrying an outcome enum (matched_approval / injected_as_input / recorded_only / rejected / error) and optional detail.
2. Outcome frame schema is documented in MOBILE_WS_PROTOCOL.md so the client knows what to deserialize.
3. The five outcome types each have a defined client-side UI behavior (dismiss, transition, brief indicator, error chip, etc.) - exact visual is mobile's call but at least one must be visible per outcome.
4. End-to-end repro: tap an A2UI Button in any chat. Within 500ms the surface visibly reacts (changes state, dismisses, shows an indicator, etc.). User can tell something happened.
5. A logcat line on the client confirms the outcome was received and dispatched to UI: 'A2UI: user_action_outcome received frameId=<id> outcome=<enum>'.
6. Errors are user-readable: 'no agent listening', 'approval gate timeout', etc., not stack traces.
7. Cross-link: a sibling bead in letta-mobile rig captures the renderer-side UI changes.
close_reason: Implemented user_action_outcome frames for approval, synthetic input, recorded-only, rejected, and error paths; validated with typecheck, build, focused A2UI tests, and full admin-shim suite.

title: Phase 5c: route non-approval A2UI user_action as synthetic user message into agent input
description:
Phase 5c: route non-approval A2UI user_action frames into agent input as conversational signal.

Today, the shim's handleUserAction in admin-shim/lib/mobile-channel-host.ts records inbound user_action frames to a sidecar and either (a) routes them through the dispatcher gate (lcp-uo5.8 / uo5.12) when they correlate with a pending tool approval, or (b) records them with no further effect when they don't. Case (b) is the gap.

For any A2UI surface that is NOT a tool approval (form submissions, dismiss actions, generic confirm/cancel buttons, etc.), the user's tap is currently conversation-invisible. The agent never sees the action, never gets a turn triggered by it, and cannot respond.

Verified end-to-end 2026-05-17 19:25 EDT on Pixel 9 Pro PID 15524: tapping a primary Button on surface final-roundtrip-test-btn with event=a2ui.final.submit produced 5 user_action frames sent cleanly over the WS (Button onClick + ChannelTransport user_action sent + submitA2uiAction result=Sent for each tap). Meridian agent received nothing and could not reply. The chain breaks at the shim layer.

Desired behavior:

When handleUserAction receives a user_action frame:

1. Try to match it against any pending tool-approval correlation (existing uo5.8 / uo5.12 path). If matched, resolve the approval as today.

2. Otherwise (no pending approval), construct a synthetic user message representing the action and inject it as the agent's next-turn input. The synthetic message should be deterministic and machine-readable - the agent should be able to recognize it as an A2UI action and not confuse it with literal user text.

Suggested synthetic message shape (open to discussion):

  [system: A2UI user action]
  surfaceId: <id>
  componentId: <id>
  event: <event.name>
  context: <serialized event.context JSON>

Or alternatively, expose it as a structured tool-call-like message_type so the agent's prompt template can render it differently from plain user text. Whichever shape lands, document it so agents that consume A2UI know what to expect.

Why this matters:

Without this bridge, A2UI's value proposition collapses to "tool approval cards only" - useful, but a small fraction of what dynamic UI is for. Forms, choice pickers, confirm/cancel modals, anything where the user provides input that should drive the next agent turn - all of those depend on this routing.

The dispatcher gate from uo5.8 / uo5.12 covers the structured-approval case. This bead covers the freeform-action case. Together they're the full Phase 5 user_action ingestion story.

Likely surfaces:

- admin-shim/lib/mobile-channel-host.ts handleUserAction - add the post-gate "if no correlation, inject as input" branch.
- The agent-pool worker spawn or the next-turn input plumbing - the synthetic message needs to land in the same queue that normal user_message frames feed into.
- Possibly a small extension to letta-code's headless stdin protocol if the synthetic message uses a non-standard shape.

Diagnostic gate:

After this lands, emitting an A2UI surface with a non-approval Button from any agent chat, tapping it, and observing the agent respond to the action within one turn is the verification. Today that response never comes.

Non-goals:

- Approval-flow routing (already covered by uo5.8 / uo5.12).
- A2UI updateDataModel feedback loops (separate concern; data-model delivery is explicitly deferred per the shim's session policy).
- Rich agent UX for handling A2UI actions (the agent decides what to do; this bead is purely about delivering the signal).

Rollback signal:

If the synthetic message confuses agents into thinking the user typed the action literally (e.g. agent responds "I see you typed a2ui.final.submit" instead of recognizing the action), revert and re-spec the message shape. The shape must be unambiguous and consistently recognizable.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Inbound user_action frames that do NOT correlate with a pending tool approval are routed into the agent's next-turn input as a synthetic user message with a documented shape (surfaceId, componentId, event name, context).
2. End-to-end repro: emit a non-approval Button from any chat, tap it, observe the agent receives input and produces a response within one turn (today: silence).
3. The existing approval-correlation path (uo5.8 / uo5.12) remains unchanged; this bead is purely the additive non-approval branch.
4. The synthetic message shape is unambiguous - documented in MOBILE_WS_PROTOCOL.md (or equivalent) so agents know how to recognize and respond to A2UI actions vs. literal user text.
5. A test fixture verifies a sample non-approval user_action produces an agent turn.
6. Logging at the shim surfaces the routing decision per inbound frame: 'matched approval', 'injected as input', 'recorded only (configured opt-out)'.
close_reason: Implemented non-approval A2UI user_action routing as synthetic agent turns over the mobile WS channel, documented the synthetic message shape, preserved sidecar recording, and added focused regression coverage.

title: Phase 5: Dispatcher approval gate (tool execution blocker)
description:
## Goal

Implement the dispatcher approval gate (Phase 5 of lcp-uo5 epic) that intercepts `approval_request_message` frames from letta-code's tool dispatcher and blocks tool execution until a user decision arrives via the mobile WS channel.

This is the **server-side gate logic** that unblocks lcp-uo5.7 (end-to-end vertical slice).

## Architecture

### Gate Insertion Point: agent-pool.ts:collector() callback (RECOMMENDED)

**Why here?**
- Intercepts `approval_request_message` frames BEFORE forwarding to onFrame handlers
- Access to runHandle, worker state, and turn context
- Blocks tool execution at the source; no need to intercept letta-code subprocess
- Single point of control for all approval decisions

**Location:** admin-shim/lib/agent-pool.ts line 420 (after frame collection, before onFrame dispatch)

### Scope Semantics

Four approval scopes with persistence:
- **Once**: Single tool call approved; decision not persisted
- **Session**: All calls to this tool in this conversation approved; persisted in sidecar
- **Forever**: All calls to this tool across all conversations approved; persisted in sidecar
- **Deny**: Tool call rejected; execution blocked; error returned to agent

### Sidecar Recording Format

Append-only JSONL file: `state/runs/<run-id>/approval-decisions.jsonl`

Each line:
```json
{
  "action_id": "uuid",
  "tool_name": "bash",
  "decision": "approve|deny|timeout",
  "scope": "Once|Session|Forever",
  "reason": "user approved",
  "timestamp": "2026-05-17T16:00:00Z",
  "user_id": "mobile-user-1"
}
```

### Timeout & Disconnect Safety

- **Approval timeout:** 30s per approval request (separate from turn timeout)
- **On timeout:** Auto-deny; record decision with reason="timeout"; return error to agent
- **On disconnect:** Worker SIGTERM handler already flips run status to "cancelled"; gate must not deadlock
- **Polling loop:** Existing 50ms polling in agent-pool.ts line 532 continues; gate waits on Promise that resolves when decision arrives or timeout fires

### Scope Persistence Query

At turn-start (agent-pool.ts:runTurn line 328):
1. Query sidecar for approval-decisions.jsonl entries with scope=Session or Forever
2. Build in-memory cache: `{ tool_name: { scope, timestamp } }`
3. On approval_request_message: check cache; if hit and scope=Session/Forever, auto-approve without user round-trip
4. If cache miss or scope=Once: wait for user_action frame from mobile WS

## Implementation Tasks

### Phase 1: Gate Logic + Sidecar Recording

- [ ] **agent-pool.ts:collector()** — Detect approval_request_message; create approval gate Promise
- [ ] **agent-pool.ts:runTurn()** — Load scope cache from sidecar at turn-start
- [ ] **runs.ts:recordApprovalDecision()** — New function to append approval decision to sidecar JSONL
- [ ] **Timeout handler** — 30s timer; auto-deny on expiry; record decision
- [ ] **Disconnect safety** — Ensure gate Promise resolves on worker SIGTERM; no deadlock

### Phase 2: Mobile WS Integration (lcp-uo5.7)

- [ ] **mobile-channel-host.ts:handleUserAction()** — Route user_action frame to gate Promise resolver
- [ ] **ws-handler.mjs** — Parse user_action frame; extract decision + scope
- [ ] **End-to-end test** — Verify approval flow with real agent + mobile client

## Files to Modify

- **admin-shim/lib/agent-pool.ts** — Gate logic, scope cache, timeout handler
- **admin-shim/lib/runs.ts** — recordApprovalDecision() function
- **admin-shim/lib/mobile-channel-host.ts** — handleUserAction() hook (Phase 2)
- **admin-shim/test/fixtures/stream-traces/** — New interactive-mode.jsonl trace with permission_mode="" (no auto_approval)

## Risks & Mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- |
| Deadlock on disconnect | Worker SIGTERM handler resolves gate Promise with error; gate checks worker.finished before waiting |
| Timeout fires after decision arrives | Gate Promise resolves on first event (decision or timeout); subsequent events ignored |
| Scope cache stale across turns | Reload cache at turn-start; append-only sidecar ensures consistency |
| Sidecar write race | JSONL append is atomic; no read-modify-write |
| Tool execution continues after deny | Gate returns error to letta-code; tool dispatcher respects error; no execution |

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Gate intercepts approval_request_message without deadlock
- [ ] Timeout fires after 30s; auto-deny recorded
- [ ] Scope cache loads correctly; Session/Forever decisions auto-approve
- [ ] Sidecar JSONL records all decisions with correct fields
- [ ] Disconnect during approval wait does not deadlock
- [ ] Unit tests pass for gate logic, timeout, scope cache, sidecar recording
- [ ] Integration test: mobile sends user_action → gate unblocks → tool executes

## Dependencies

- Phases 1-4 of lcp-uo5 (schema injection, splitter, validation, WS protocol)
- lcp-uo5.7 (end-to-end vertical slice) depends on this

## References

- **Architecture map:** See HANDOFF.md (locked contracts section)
- **Mock trace:** admin-shim/test/fixtures/stream-traces/bash-tool.jsonl (approval_request_message example)
- **Scope semantics:** Defined in lcp-uo5 epic description
- **Turn lifecycle:** agent-pool.ts:runTurn() line 328; polling loop line 532
- **Worker pool:** agent-pool.ts:Worker class; SIGTERM handler line 357
close_reason: Implemented approval_request gate wiring, mobile user_action decision routing, Once/Session/Deny/timeout handling, approvals.json policy cache, and decision audit sidecars; validated with focused and full admin-shim tests.

title: A2UI catalogId contradiction: negotiation declares 'basic', embedded schema declares URL form
description:
The shim tells the model two different catalogIds in the same system prompt:

1. Session-capability line says: catalogId='basic' (a2ui-adapter.ts:4 DEFAULT_A2UI_CATALOG_ID, surfaced via buildA2uiSystemPrompt:117).
2. The embedded basic_catalog.json schema (a2ui-v09-basic-prompt.ts) declares catalogId='https://a2ui.org/specification/v0_9/basic_catalog.json'.

When the model emits createSurface, it can pick either, depending on recency. validateA2uiMessage (a2ui-stream-splitter.ts:198) does not even check that the emitted catalogId matches what was negotiated, so both shapes silently pass through.

Two fixes — pick one:

(a) Adopt the URL form on the wire. Change DEFAULT_A2UI_CATALOG_ID + negotiation + mobile side to use 'https://a2ui.org/specification/v0_9/basic_catalog.json'. Pro: interop with stock A2UI tooling. Con: long opaque string on the wire.

(b) Rewrite the schema's catalogId at prompt-build time to match our short slug. In buildA2uiSystemPrompt, string-replace the upstream catalogId URL with 'basic' inside the embedded schema. Pro: keeps wire-tight slug. Con: prompt diverges from upstream Apache-licensed SDK output; can drift on SDK regen.

Additionally, validateA2uiMessage should reject createSurface messages whose catalogId doesn't match the negotiated capability — currently we accept any non-empty string.
close_reason: Resolved catalogId contradiction by rewriting the embedded Basic Catalog prompt to the negotiated short slug and validating createSurface.catalogId against the negotiated capability.

title: A2UI supportedWidgets advertises 3 widgets not in Basic Catalog (Form, StatusBeacon, ToolApprovalCard)
description:
The shim's server capabilities (admin-shim/lib/a2ui-adapter.ts:45-55) advertise 'Form', 'StatusBeacon', 'ToolApprovalCard' as supported widgets, but none of these exist in the upstream A2UI v0.9 Basic Catalog (basic_catalog.json embedded in admin-shim/lib/a2ui-v09-basic-prompt.ts).

Real Basic Catalog widgets: Text, Image, Icon, Video, AudioPlayer, Row, Column, List, Card, Tabs, Modal, Divider, Button, TextField, CheckBox, ChoicePicker, Slider, DateTimeInput.

This produces two contradictions inside our own system prompt:
1. The capability-negotiation line tells the model 'the client renders Form, StatusBeacon, ToolApprovalCard' (a2ui-adapter.ts:107-117 buildA2uiSystemPrompt).
2. The embedded schema's anyComponent.oneOf does NOT include them.

Net effect: model is encouraged to emit widgets that the schema rejects.

ToolApprovalCard belongs in a separate custom Letta catalog with its own catalogId (per docs/A2UI_DECISION_LOG.md:36-38 'Custom Letta-specific widgets should be designed in a separate epic'). Form and StatusBeacon don't appear to belong anywhere — they may be confused with HTML primitives.

Fix: trim A2UI_DEFAULT_SUPPORTED_WIDGETS in a2ui-adapter.ts to the Basic Catalog subset the mobile renderer actually mounts. Initial set: Text, Button, Card, List, TextField, ChoicePicker. Defer ToolApprovalCard until the custom-catalog epic.
close_reason: Trimmed advertised A2UI widgets to the Basic Catalog subset and filtered runtime client widget declarations before prompt injection.

title: listAllConversations cache stale after last_message_at bump
description:
Mobile conversations list shows stale last_message_at because the dir-mtime cache (lcp-5e5) only invalidates when a conv dir is added or removed — content-only writes to conversation.json (the bump path in bumpConversationLastMessageAt) don't change the parent dir's mtime, so the cached list keeps serving stale timestamps.

Repro: send a message via mobile WS → conversation.json on disk has the fresh last_message_at, but GET /v1/conversations returns the old value until a new conv is created.

Fix: expose invalidate() on makeDirMtimeCache and call it from bumpConversationLastMessageAt so the bump path drops the cache. listAgents has the same caveat but no current writer mutates agent.json fields the list cares about — defer that side.

title: Phase 5b: wire user_action to tool dispatcher gate (Once/Session/Forever/Deny + timeout)
description:
Phase 5 wire-up: user action to dispatcher gate.

Current state in mobile-channel-host.ts: user action frames are recorded to a sidecar but the tool dispatcher does not consult it. Without the gate, lcp-uo5.7 vertical slice cannot pass.

Desired: dispatcher blocks at approval point, ToolApprovalCard emits, shim waits for user action correlated by run_id and tool_call_id. Resolutions: Once/Session/Forever/Deny + 30s timeout default to Deny.

Surfaces: mobile-channel-host.ts handleUserAction resolves pending promise; agent-pool.ts gains wait-for-approval primitive; approvals.json persists session/forever decisions.

Non-goals: multi-user approval, delegation, cross-rig renderer changes.

Rollback: if dispatcher deadlocks on disconnect without user action, revert.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Round-trip test: agent calls gated tool, ToolApprovalCard emits, mock client sends user_action(scope=Once), tool runs.
2. Scope=Session: second invocation in same session auto-approves.
3. Scope=Forever: persists in approvals.json; fresh session also auto-approves.
4. Scope=Deny: tool refuses with recoverable error.
5. Timeout: configurable via A2UI_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_MS; defaults to Deny-equivalent at 30s.
6. Audit log entries exist for all five decisions.
7. Client disconnect mid-approval resolves via timeout within timeout+100ms (no deadlock).
8. Phase 5 sidecar recording path remains intact for observability.
notes: Current local state: user_action remains recording/ack only; sidecar path is intact and sendDataModel=true is now rejected to avoid silent data loss. Full closure still requires a stable letta-code tool-dispatcher approval API for Once/Session/Forever/Deny/timeout semantics.

title: Phase 6: End-to-end vertical slice — ToolApprovalCard round-trip
description:
## Goal

Demonstrate the entire shim emission story end-to-end with a real Letta agent and a real renderer (letta-mobile rig): agent emits ToolApprovalCard → shim parses/validates/forwards → renderer displays → user taps → action flows back → agent's tool dispatcher unblocks with the correct scope decision.

This is **the milestone moment**. Everything in Phases 1-5 builds toward this single proof point.

## Background

This ticket lives in the letta rig but its acceptance criteria require coordinated work in the letta-mobile rig. The renderer-side ticket should be filed in letta-mobile and cross-referenced.

## Tasks

- [ ] Pick a Letta test agent and a real destructive tool to gate (e.g., `bash` with a rm-like command)
- [ ] Configure the tool to require approval
- [ ] Wire up the A2UI capability on the test agent
- [ ] End-to-end test scenario:
  1. User on Android: "Please delete /tmp/junk for me"
  2. Agent decides to call `bash rm -rf /tmp/junk`
  3. Tool dispatcher blocks; agent emits ToolApprovalCard A2UI message
  4. Shim parses, validates, forwards over WS
  5. Renderer displays card with tool=bash, args, risk=destructive, 4 affordances
  6. User taps "Once"
  7. userAction flows back through shim
  8. Tool gate unblocks; bash runs once; result returned to agent
  9. Agent responds with confirmation text + StatusBeacon showing success
- [ ] Repeat with each of 4 scope choices, verify all behave correctly
- [ ] Repeat with timeout (no user response in 30s) — verify auto-deny
- [ ] Verify audit log entries

## Acceptance criteria

- All 4 scope decisions work end-to-end with real Sonnet driving real agent
- Timeout works
- No flakes across 10 consecutive runs
- Latency budget: card appears in app within 2s of user prompt; tool executes within 1s of approval tap

## Risks

- This is integration work; depends on letta-mobile rig progressing in parallel
- May surface design issues in earlier phases that require revisits — that's the point of vertical slices

## Dependencies

- Phases 1-5 in this rig
- Cross-rig: letta-mobile ToolApprovalCard widget implementation + WS frame parsing

notes: Server-side dispatcher gate is now implemented and locally validated: approval_request_message forwards to mobile, waits for user_action, writes approval-decisions.jsonl, supports Session policy cache in approvals.json, Deny, and configurable timeout. Remaining blocker is real letta-mobile ToolApprovalCard renderer/WS parsing plus live Sonnet/Android vertical-slice validation across 10 runs.

title: Phase 5: userAction handler + tool dispatcher gate
description:
## Goal

Receive `userAction` events from the client (button taps, form submissions, approval choices), route them to the right destination — most importantly, gate the agent's tool dispatcher on tool-approval responses with correct scope semantics.

## Background

This is **the thing that killed Matrix-as-primary**. Matrix can't do synchronous tool approval; A2UI + WS can. The pattern from Agentic Launcher (AAOSP): scope choices are **Once / This chat / Always / Deny**.

When the agent wants to call a tool that requires approval, it emits a `ToolApprovalCard` A2UI message (callId is opaque, sent back with the userAction). The shim:
1. Holds the tool call in pending state
2. Forwards the card to the client (Phase 4)
3. Waits for the userAction with matching callId
4. Applies the scope decision and either executes the tool or returns denial to the agent

## Tasks

- [ ] Define userAction frame format on client→shim WS direction
  - Fields: `actionName`, `surfaceId`, `context` (dict, varies by widget)
  - For tool approval: `actionName=tool_approval_response`, `context={callId, decision, scope}`
- [ ] Implement pending tool-call registry keyed by callId
- [ ] Implement scope grant store (per-agent, per-conversation, per-user)
  - Once: consumed on next call
  - Session: cleared on conversation reset
  - Forever: persisted (revocable via admin UI later)
  - Deny: tool call returns error to agent, agent decides next move
- [ ] Implement timeout: if no userAction within N seconds, auto-deny + emit timeout message
- [ ] Audit log: every approval decision (granted/denied, scope, callId, tool, args) logged for later inspection
- [ ] Test with a destructive tool (e.g., `bash rm -rf /tmp/test`) — verify the agent blocks until user responds

## Acceptance criteria

- A tool marked `requires_approval` causes the agent to emit a ToolApprovalCard and block
- User taps any of the 4 affordances; the shim unblocks the agent appropriately
- Scope grants persist correctly (Once/Session/Forever) and are correctly consulted on subsequent calls
- Audit log captures every approval decision
- Timeout (default 30s) auto-denies and notifies the agent

## Risks

- Persistent storage of Forever grants — where does this live? (Recommend: Letta server, attached to agent metadata)
- Race conditions between tool dispatch and userAction arrival (handle via the callId registry being authoritative)

## Dependencies

- Phase 4 (WS protocol must carry userAction client→shim)
- Cross-rig: ToolApprovalCard widget must be implemented in letta-mobile renderer

## Reported by

Meridian + Emmanuel

title: Phase 4: WS frame protocol for A2UI delivery
description:
## Goal

Define how A2UI frames are delivered to mobile clients over our existing WebSocket transport. Frames must be interleaved correctly with existing text deltas, ordered, and identifiable so the renderer can dispatch them to the correct surface.

## Background

The new mobile transport (commits 3ac9733 onward) already streams text + tool-call events over WS. A2UI introduces additional frame types that need to ride on the same WS without breaking existing clients.

Existing frame types (rough):
- text_delta
- tool_call_start
- tool_call_arguments_delta
- tool_call_result
- turn_done

New A2UI frame types needed:
- a2ui_create_surface
- a2ui_update_components
- a2ui_update_data_model
- a2ui_delete_surface
- a2ui_action_ack  (server confirms received user action)

## Tasks

- [ ] Design the WS envelope for A2UI frames (recommend: a single `a2ui` event type with the A2UI message as payload, so we don't pollute the event-type space)
- [ ] Update WS protocol docs (admin-shim, letta-mobile)
- [ ] Implement server-side emission of A2UI events in the WS stream
- [ ] Coordinate frame versioning so old clients receiving new event types degrade gracefully (just ignore unknown events)
- [ ] Add a `a2ui_capabilities` server→client message sent right after handshake to confirm A2UI is active for this session

## Acceptance criteria

- A2UI frames flow over the same WS connection as text/tool events
- Non-A2UI clients on the same shim are unaffected (no new event types they don't expect)
- Frame ordering matches LLM emission order (text segments and A2UI messages stay sequenced)
- Documented in admin-shim repo as part of the WS protocol

## Risks

- Coordination with letta-mobile rig: the renderer must understand the envelope we send. Lock the envelope schema BEFORE either side hardens implementation.
- Backward compatibility: old client binaries should not break when shim adds a2ui events to the stream

## Dependencies

- Phase 2 (splitter)
- Phase 3 (validation)
- Cross-rig: matching renderer-side parse logic in letta-mobile rig (to be filed separately)

## Reported by

Meridian + Emmanuel

title: Phase 1: Schema injection + capability negotiation
description:
## Goal

Add capability negotiation to the shim so that mobile clients can declare A2UI support, and inject the A2UI catalog schema + workflow rules into the upstream system prompt when negotiated.

## Background

The Python SDK's `A2uiSchemaManager.generate_system_prompt()` produces a ~13K-token grammar pack (role description + UI description + full JSON schema + 18-component catalog + 4 validated example messages). We proved May 16 that this makes sonnet-4-5 emit valid A2UI on first try.

For the shim, this needs to:
1. Happen lazily — only when the client signals it can render A2UI
2. Be cached aggressively — Anthropic prompt caching reduces the recurring cost
3. Be configurable — different agents may want different catalogs/widgets

## Tasks

- [ ] Create `llmux_shim/a2ui_adapter.py` module
- [ ] Define capability negotiation message format (client→shim handshake)
  - Suggested: an extension to existing WS handshake or a sentinel header on first chat request
  - Fields: `a2ui_version`, `supported_catalogs`, `supported_widgets`, `theme_hints`
- [ ] Implement schema injection: when capability negotiated, prepend A2UI grammar block to system prompt
- [ ] Verify Anthropic `cache_control` headers pass through correctly so the grammar block is cached
- [ ] Add config knob: `A2UI_ENABLED`, `A2UI_CATALOG_ID`, `A2UI_VERSION` env vars
- [ ] Make the role_description + ui_description configurable per agent (likely from agent metadata, not shim config)

## Acceptance criteria

- A client can announce A2UI capability and receive A2UI-enabled responses from the upstream model via the shim
- A client that does NOT announce capability gets plain text responses (no behavior change)
- Schema-pack tokens are cached across requests in a session (verify via Anthropic usage reporting)
- Unit test: capability handshake produces expected augmented system prompt

## Risks

- Anthropic prompt caching has specific block-size minimums and TTLs; need to verify the 13K block qualifies and stays cached
- Capability handshake design needs to not break non-A2UI clients

## Dependencies

- Phase 0 (decision log)

Config knobs: A2UI_ENABLED, A2UI_VERSION, A2UI_CATALOG_ID, A2UI_ROLE_DESCRIPTION, A2UI_UI_DESCRIPTION. Tests added in admin-shim/test/a2ui-adapter.test.ts and ws-protocol.test.ts. Added WS hello negotiation fields, welcome/a2ui_capabilities confirmation, session-scoped prompt augmentation for negotiated turns, env config knobs, docs, and tests. title: Phase 2: Streaming response splitter (text vs A2UI frames)
description:
## Goal

Modify the shim's response streaming path so that responses containing inline `<a2ui-json>`...`</a2ui-json>` blocks are split: conversational text streams through as normal text deltas, A2UI blocks are extracted, parsed into individual A2UI messages, and forwarded as structured frames.

## Background

A2UI v0.9 workflow rule (from system prompt): the LLM emits conversational text interleaved with A2UI JSON blocks wrapped in `<a2ui-json>` tags. Tonight's demo showed sonnet-4-5 follows this reliably.

The Python SDK provides `a2ui.parser.parser.parse_response()` which splits a complete response into `ResponsePart` objects (each with `text` and/or `a2ui_json` fields). For streaming, we need a **streaming-capable** variant that emits parts incrementally as the LLM streams.

A2UI's design specifically supports streaming: the spec mandates "parent components MUST appear before their child components" inside `updateComponents` so the renderer can mount skeletons progressively. Our splitter must preserve this property — emit each A2UI message as a complete frame as soon as it's parseable from the byte stream.

## Tasks

- [ ] Investigate whether `a2ui.parser` has an incremental/streaming API; if not, build one in our adapter
- [ ] Design output frame types for downstream WS transport:
  - `text_delta`: streaming text token (existing path)
  - `a2ui_frame`: one complete A2UI message (createSurface, updateComponents, updateDataModel, etc.)
  - `stream_done`: end-of-response marker
- [ ] Handle malformed A2UI blocks gracefully (log + skip, don't break the text stream)
- [ ] Handle interleaved emission: text → a2ui → text → a2ui → text in any order
- [ ] Preserve token-level latency for text deltas (don't buffer text waiting for an a2ui block to close)

## Acceptance criteria

- Given a Sonnet response with 2 text segments and 3 A2UI messages, the splitter emits exactly those 5 frames in order
- Text streams at upstream's actual token rate (no buffering regression)
- A2UI frames each contain a single, valid A2UI message
- Malformed A2UI blocks log a warning but do not interrupt downstream text streaming
- Integration test using saved fixtures from May 16 demo (3 prompts, known-good responses)

## Risks

- Streaming parser is harder than batch parser; need to handle byte boundaries mid-tag, mid-JSON
- Backpressure: if client is slow, do we buffer or drop?

## Dependencies

- Phase 1 (schema injection so LLM actually produces A2UI)

## Reported by

Meridian + Emmanuel

title: Epic: A2UI agent emission via llmux shim
description:
## Summary

Make the llmux shim capable of emitting A2UI (Agent-to-User Interface) protocol messages alongside conventional text responses, so that Letta agents can drive a rich dynamic UI surface (initially on Android). This is the **server-side half** of the dynamic UI initiative — the **client-side half** lives in the `letta-mobile` rig.

## Context

Decided May 16, 2026 after extended architecture session and successful end-to-end demo against Google's A2UI v0.9 spec driven by sonnet-4-5 through the existing shim. Three different surface types (booking form, confirmation card, list) all emitted with 100% schema-valid output on first try.

Key references:
- A2UI spec: https://a2ui.org
- A2UI repo (cloned to /tmp/a2ui-demo): https://github.com/google/A2UI
- Demo evidence: ~13K token system prompt, 10-17s latency, 3/3 valid
- Architecture decision: Matrix becomes side window for audit/notification, NOT primary agent transport. Android (Letta Mobile) becomes the primary rich UI surface. Tool approval flows run over our WS transport, NOT Matrix.

## Goals for this epic

The shim becomes able to:
1. Inject the A2UI catalog schema + workflow rules into the upstream model's system prompt on demand (capability-negotiated per session)
2. Parse the streamed response to separate conversational text from `<a2ui-json>` blocks
3. Validate A2UI messages server-side before forwarding to clients
4. Forward A2UI frames over the existing mobile WS transport in a way the renderer can consume
5. Route `userAction` messages from the client back to the agent's tool dispatcher with correct semantics (especially for tool-approval scope choices: Once / Session / Forever / Deny)

## Non-goals

- The renderer itself (lives in letta-mobile rig)
- Matrix degradation (deferred to later phase)
- Custom Letta widget catalog beyond v1 essentials
- Production hardening, theming
- Multi-agent UI orchestration (deferred)

## Success criteria (epic-level)

End-to-end vertical slice: a Letta agent emits a ToolApprovalCard A2UI message. The shim parses, validates, forwards to mobile client over WS. User taps Approve in Android renderer. Action flows back through shim and unblocks the agent's tool dispatcher with the correct scope.

That single slice proves: schema injection works, parse/validate works, frame forwarding works, action routing works, tool gate works.

## Phases

- **Phase 0:** Local A2UI Python SDK eval + decisions (small, mostly already done in May 16 session)
- **Phase 1:** Schema injection + capability negotiation
- **Phase 2:** Streaming response splitter (text vs a2ui frames)
- **Phase 3:** Server-side schema validation + error handling
- **Phase 4:** WS frame protocol for A2UI delivery to client
- **Phase 5:** userAction handler + tool dispatcher gate
- **Phase 6:** Vertical slice integration test (with letta-mobile rig)

## Open questions

- Where does the A2UI adapter live? In llmux_shim/server.py directly, or as a separate module/service? Recommend: new module `a2ui_adapter.py` alongside server.py to keep the shim core focused on transport.
- Catalog: standard A2UI v0.9 Basic Catalog only for v1, OR start with custom Letta catalog from day one? Recommend: standard catalog v1, design Letta-specific widgets in a separate epic later.
- Prompt caching: confirm shim passes through Anthropic prompt-caching headers correctly so the 13K-token A2UI grammar is cached per session.

Meridian + Emmanuel, planning session May 16, 2026

title: Initial conv load: existing conversation missing from list, 'new conversation' inherits its history
description:
**Why this matters**

The initial conversation load path has two interacting bugs that together produce a silent-data-loss feel for the user:

1. An existing conversation does not appear in the chat list — the user thinks it's gone.
2. When the user creates a "new conversation" to escape the apparent loss, the new conversation opens carrying the *missing* conversation's full history (agent persona + prior messages), as though they had clicked back into the old one.

Net effect: a real conversation is invisible by its own id, but reachable as a phantom "new" conversation. The user has no reliable way to tell whether they are starting fresh or continuing an existing thread, and no path back to the conversation through its proper handle. This blocks any workflow that depends on multiple distinct conversations against the same agent.

The bug was introduced (or surfaced) in the last 24h of shim work — see hypothesis below.

**Current behavior**

Reproduced 2026-05-16 morning (user-observed):

- A conversation that previously existed and was actively used does not show up in the mobile chat list.
- Tapping "new conversation" on the same agent opens a chat that immediately loads the missing conversation's persona, system context, and full message history into the new shell.
- The user can interact with this phantom; the agent has its prior context. So the conversation is alive on disk — it's only unreachable through its own list entry.

It is unknown at this point whether:

- The conversation is missing from the listing endpoint's JSON, or present in the JSON but filtered client-side.
- The "new conversation" flow is creating a fresh on-disk conv that the resolver immediately maps to the existing one, or whether it is short-circuiting and never creating a new record at all.
- The two symptoms are one bug or two.

**Hypothesis (start here)**

Two commits landed in the last 24h that both touched the load / projection path:

1. **`0ef20bf` — `fix: messages.jsonl schema migration + turn_done error fields + stderr-on-exit`.** Schema migrations on the load path are a high-likelihood source of "first-load-after-deploy" bugs. If the migration mutates the on-disk conversation id (or any field the resolver matches on), the conversation may now resolve under a new id that the listing endpoint exposes but mobile's stored handle does not know about. Mobile would then fail to find its conv in the list, and the "new conversation" id mobile sends would be matched to the existing conv by the resolver's fallback path. **This is the leading suspect.**

2. **`3794da2` — `lcp-nwd: project run_id on messages so mobile run-grouping works`.** Less likely as a root cause (it adds a field; it does not change resolution), but `buildMessageRunMap` is now called on every initial-load endpoint (`handleAgentContext`, `handleAgentMessages`, `handleConversationMessagesList`). If conversation resolution silently picks the wrong conv, the run-attribution projection will succeed against the wrong messages — making the wrong-conv-load look "correct" to mobile and harder to detect.

The conversation-id resolver in `admin-shim/lib/store.ts` (or wherever `resolveConversationId` lives now) accepts both internal `conv-<uuid>` and external `conv-default-<agentId>` forms, and falls back to the client's pair if neither resolves. That fallback is the most likely site of the bug — a stale or ambiguous id from mobile may be falling through to "use this existing conv" rather than "create a new one."

**Diagnostic checklist (run these in order before changing code)**

1. **Disk state.** Inspect the conversations directory on the shim host. Count the per-conv directories and confirm the missing-from-list conversation is still present as its own record (not merged, not renamed):
   ```sh
   ls -la /opt/stacks/letta-code-parallel/home/.letta/conversations/ 2>/dev/null || \
     find /opt/stacks/letta-code-parallel/home/.letta -type d -name "conv-*" -maxdepth 4
   ```
2. **List endpoint.** Hit the shim directly with the agent id from mobile and check whether the conv appears at all and under what id:
   ```sh
   curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/agents/<agentId>/conversations | jq '[.[] | {id, agent_id, created_at}]'
   curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/conversations | jq '[.[] | {id, agent_id, created_at}]'
   ```
3. **Mobile request log.** Capture the exact `conversation_id` mobile sends when the user taps "new conversation" (logcat or shim's access log). Then trace that id through `resolveConversationId` and confirm whether it resolves to the existing conv via the fallback path.

If the conv is present on disk and present in the listing endpoint's JSON but missing in mobile, the bug is mobile-side. If the conv is missing from the listing endpoint's JSON but present on disk, the bug is in the listing handler or its filter. If "new conv" requests resolve to the existing conv id, the bug is in the resolver fallback.

**Desired behavior**

- The conversation is visible in the listing endpoint for its agent under its canonical id.
- Tapping "new conversation" creates a genuinely new conversation on disk and the mobile UI opens an empty chat — no inherited persona, no inherited history.
- Existing conversations remain reachable through their stored handles across mobile restarts.
- The schema migration (`0ef20bf`) leaves the conversation-id stable so mobile's stored handles remain valid.

**Non-goals**

- Adding a "show archived conversations" toggle or any visibility setting — this is about a conv that should be visible and isn't.
- Migrating the message schema back out — keep the new schema, fix the load path.
- Improving the conversation list's UI sort/group affordances — out of scope.
- Multi-account conversation isolation — out of scope.

**Rollback signal**

If a fix re-binds the conv to a different id (even silently) to "make it appear" in the list, revert. The user has stored handles to the old id; any rename without an explicit migration ack breaks resume-from-history. Acceptable fixes either preserve the original id on disk and in the listing, or perform an explicit id migration with a visible upgrade path.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The exact reproduction sequence is captured as an automated regression test: deploy shim → open conversation A → close client → re-open client → list contains A under its original id.
2. The "new conversation" flow against the same agent creates an empty chat on disk and renders empty on mobile — no persona, system context, or history is inherited from any existing conversation.
3. A regression test exists for the schema-migration code path: a `messages.jsonl` file written under the pre-`0ef20bf` schema is loaded; the conversation appears in the listing endpoint under its original id; mobile's stored conv handle still resolves to it.
4. The `resolveConversationId` fallback path is documented: every fallback case explicitly states which id it resolves to and why. Where the current behavior is "fall through to client's pair," the bead implementer either confirms that path is correct or replaces it with a narrower rule that does not produce a wrong-conv match.
5. The lcp-nwd `run_id` projection path is verified intact: a load of the now-visible conversation continues to carry `run_id` on every message that was attributed to a run, identical to pre-fix behavior.
6. The fix does not silently re-key, rename, or merge any conversation. If any id mutation is required, it is performed by an explicit migration step that is logged at INFO level, called out in the commit message, and covered by its own test.

title: Shim listMessages misses post-migration records: parts -> content schema bump
description:
letta-code's {
  "storageDir": "/root/.letta/lc-local-backend",
  "converted": [],
  "skipped": [],
  "dryRun": false
} (run today on 2026-05-15) renamed the messages.jsonl per-line field from `parts` (legacy) to `content` (current). The shim's isLocalMessage filter required `parts` to be an array, so every migrated record was filtered out and GET /v1/conversations/<id>/messages returned [] for any conversation that had been migrated.

Symptom on mobile: message history disappeared after the migration ran; conversation list showed last activity months in the past because conversation.json's last_message_at was also reset to the migrator's sentinel (2026-01-01T...).

Fix:
- store.ts isLocalMessage: accept either parts OR content.
- store.ts normalizeMessage(record): mirror content -> parts when parts is missing.
- store.ts listMessages: items.map(normalizeMessage).filter(isLocalMessage) before downstream consumers see the records.
- Backfill: re-run scripts/backfill-last-message-at.mjs (computed max from _real-times.json sidecar, which the migration didn't touch).

The post-migration on-disk schema is otherwise field-identical for our reads (same element shape {type:"text", text:...}); just the field name changed. Old .pre-pi-backup-YYYY-... files still readable via the same code path (legacy parts form).

Acceptance: a conversation that has been migrated returns its full message history via GET /v1/conversations/<id>/messages. Mobile chat UI shows actual history again. last_message_at sorted to the top of the conversation list reflects real recent activity.

Regression test: seed a messages.jsonl with the new schema (content array, no parts), confirm listMessages returns the message AND that the projected wire shape has the same text body as the legacy form.

title: Messages projected without run_id — breaks mobile run-grouping in chat UI
description:
Every wire projection in admin-shim/lib/translate.ts hardcodes run_id: null on emitted LettaMessages:

  - localMessageToConversationMessages (used by GET /v1/conversations/{id}/messages): 7 hardcoded null run_id assignments at lines 391, 415, 448, 483, 515, 551, 597.
  - localMessageToLettaMessage (LegacyLocalMessageWire — used by GET /v1/agents/{id}/messages and the conversation create response): no run_id field at all.

Mobile's chat UI groups bubbles by run_id for the collapsible 'run blocks' affordance. With run_id null on every message, every message renders ungrouped. Vanilla Letta server populates run_id from its own ORM, so mobile's grouping works against letta.oculair.ca but not against the parallel shim.

Fix:
- Build an inverse messageId -> runId map by walking listRuns({ agentId, conversationId }) and indexing run.message_ids[]. Same data is already on disk; just needs a reader.
- Extend LocalMessageScope with runIdsByMessageId?: Record<string,string> | null.
- Substitute scope.runIdsByMessageId?.[localMsg.id] for the hardcoded null at every emission site in localMessageToConversationMessages.
- Extend LegacyLocalMessageWire (and localMessageToLettaMessage) with run_id: string | null sourced the same way.
- Update server.ts handleConversationMessagesList + handleAgentMessages to build the map (scoped to internal conv id + agent id) and pass via scope.

Acceptance: GET /v1/conversations/<conv>/messages returns each message with run_id set when a run attributed it. Mobile chat UI collapses by run on the shim path same as on vanilla Letta.

title: WS: add turn_done.lossy flag for backpressure-dropped frames
description:
From contract review: the shim currently drops individual frames silently when ws.bufferedAmount > bufferHighWaterBytes. Mobile has no signal that any drop happened, so it would have to reconcile defensively after every turn — undoing most of the point of streaming.

Proposed:
- ws-handler.mjs tracks a per-turn drop counter inside the send_message handler closure
- on turn_done emission, include lossy: bool (true iff drops > 0)
- optionally include drop_count: number for telemetry

Mobile contract: when turn_done.lossy === true, run a reconcile pass for the turn; otherwise skip. Captures the recovery semantics declaratively.

Spec section to update in MOBILE_WS_STREAMING_CONTRACT.md: 'Backpressure'. Plus the turn_done frame fields table.

title: WS: cancel-during-startup gap — guarantee run_id on turn_started OR define client-buffer behavior
description:
From contract review: ChannelTransport.cancel() returns false between turn_started and the first run_id-bearing frame because there is no run_id yet to send. lcp-bll requires cancel.run_id to be present (no implicit fallback). Two compatible options to close the gap:

A) Shim always creates the run BEFORE writing turn_started, so turn_started always carries run_id. Mobile can cancel immediately on turn_started.

B) Spec adds a normative 'client MUST buffer cancel until the first run_id-bearing frame arrives, then dispatch.'

Recommended: (A) — verifiable via test, no client state machine required. Need to confirm where the run handle is created in agent-pool.ts and whether emitting turn_started can be deferred until after onRunCreated fires.

Acceptance: turn_started.run_id is non-null on every send_message → turn_started transition. New test: ws: turn_started always carries non-null run_id.

title: mobile WS channel coalesces assistant_message instead of streaming chunks
description:
bridgeSendMessage in lib/mobile-channel-host.ts server-side-coalesces assistant_message chunks (pendingAssistant + chunkBuffer) and emits ONE final assistant_message per turn. Mobile expects PURE DELTAS per the lettabot-uww.11 contract: each chunk arrives separately, mobile finds the existing event by serverId, appends new content. With the current coalescing the user sees the entire reply pop in at once instead of streaming.

Fix:
- Remove the pendingAssistant/chunkBuffer logic in bridgeSendMessage.
- For assistant_message frames with otid, set frame.id = 'cm-stream-' + otid so every chunk merges by serverId on mobile.
- For reasoning_message, same pattern (cm-reason-prefix).
- ws-handler.mjs must pass outFrame.id through to the WS envelope for these typed messages so makeFrame's randomUUID doesn't override it.
- Keep pendingStop / pendingUsage end-of-turn ordering — those should still arrive last.

Does NOT touch chat.ts coalesceAssistantFrames — that's the SSE/REST path which intentionally matches vanilla Letta's 'one assistant_message per turn' shape and has its own test coverage.

title: GET /v1/blocks returns duplicate block IDs across labels for same agent
description:
readBlocksForAgent (lib/store.ts:652) built block.id as:
  block-${b64url(`${agentId}:${label}`).slice(0, 24)}

The slice cuts at position 24, which falls inside the base64-encoded agent UUID prefix. The colon and label never make it into the truncated id, so every block on the same agent gets the SAME id.

Observed in production: 13 different blocks all sharing 'block-YWdlbnQtMmZhZTRhMjMtMWNh' (agent-2fae4a23-...), 4 more sharing 'block-YWdlbnQtNTk3YjU3NTYtMjkx' (agent-597b5756-...).

Impact: mobile blocks screen crashes with duplicate-key error (Compose LazyColumn requires unique keys).

Fix: derive id from sha256(`${agentId}:${label}`) hex, take first 24 chars. Same width as before, unique by construction, no decode needed (handleBlockDetail just iterates and compares strings).

title: perf+correctness: sidecar JSON writes are O(n) and not crash-safe
description: writeOtidForLocalId (store.mjs:218) and stampNewMessages (store.mjs:264) follow the same pattern: read whole sidecar JSON → mutate → JSON.stringify → writeFileSync. This is O(n) per turn in sidecar size and not crash-safe — a crash mid-write leaves a truncated/invalid JSON file that subsequent readJsonOrNull() will silently treat as empty, losing all otid/timestamp mappings for that conversation.
design: Two complementary changes: (1) atomic write via writeFile(tmp) + rename(tmp, final) — fsync the tmp first if we care about durability. (2) Convert sidecars to append-only JSONL: each line is {id, value}; reads fold the map by last-write-wins; periodic compaction (e.g. on conv close, or when line count > 2x distinct ids) rewrites a compact form atomically. JSONL append is O(1) per turn instead of O(n).
acceptance_criteria: Sidecar writes are atomic (no torn files visible to readers) and cost does not grow linearly with conversation length per turn.
notes:
TS migration update (2026-05-15, post-phase-7c): all referenced files renamed .mjs → .ts. Updated locations:
- store.ts:380 — writeOtidForLocalId() (was store.mjs:218)
- store.ts:433 — stampNewMessages() (was store.mjs:264)
- store.ts:374 — readOtidMap() (relevant to atomic-write redesign)
TypedSidecar interfaces likely exist now in lib/types/ — use them when designing the JSONL line shape so writers and compactors share a type.

title: perf: findUnmappedTailUserMessageId re-reads entire messages.jsonl every turn
description: After every successful WS turn, mobile-channel-host.mjs:140 calls findUnmappedTailUserMessageId() to bind the mobile-supplied otid to the user message letta-code just persisted. That function (store.mjs:239) does listMessages() which slurps the entire messages.jsonl and JSON.parses every line, then iterates from the tail. Cost grows linearly with conversation length on every single turn.
design: Best fix: have the agent-pool worker return the newly-written user message id as part of runTurn()'s result — the worker already knows what it wrote. bridgeSendMessage then calls writeOtidForLocalId() directly without scanning. Fallback: reverse-read messages.jsonl by line using a streaming tail reader instead of slurping.
acceptance_criteria: otid binding should be O(1) (or at worst O(log n)) per turn regardless of conversation length.
notes:
TS migration update (2026-05-15, post-phase-7c): all referenced files renamed .mjs → .ts. Updated locations:
- mobile-channel-host.ts ~218 — findUnmappedTailUserMessageId() call after turn (was line 140 in .mjs)
- store.ts:408 — findUnmappedTailUserMessageId() definition
- store.ts:409 — listMessages() call that slurps messages.jsonl
- store.ts:315 — listMessages() definition
Recommended fix unchanged: have agent-pool.ts worker.runTurn() return the new user message id so this scan goes away entirely.

title: perf: resolveConversationId does full disk scan on every send
description: mobile-channel-host.mjs:65 calls resolveConversationId() for every WS send_message frame. When the id is not the conv-default-<agentId> form, it falls through to listAllConversations() in store.mjs:101 — a full readdirSync + readFileSync + JSON.parse of every conversation directory. With N conversations on disk and a chatty mobile client doing M sends, this is O(N*M) syscalls + parses per session.
design: Two options: (a) lazy in-memory cache in store.mjs invalidated on mtime change of the conversations root; (b) push resolution into agent-pool worker creation so the worker holds the resolved pair for its lifetime. (b) is cleaner — the worker already keys on (convId, agentId) so it can hand the resolved pair back to bridgeSendMessage as part of getAgentPool().get().
acceptance_criteria: Resolution should be O(1) (or O(log N)) per send. Cache {externalId → {conversationId, agentId}} keyed by mtime, or stash the resolved pair on the agent-pool worker once per worker so repeat sends on the same conv hit memory.
notes:
TS migration update (2026-05-15, post-phase-7c): all referenced files renamed .mjs → .ts. Updated locations:
- mobile-channel-host.ts:131 — resolveConversationId() call in bridgeSendMessage
- store.ts:280 — resolveConversationId() definition
- store.ts:256 — listAllConversations() fallback path
- store.ts:286 — the disk scan loop inside resolveConversationId
Strict-mode is now on, so the cache implementation will need typed nullability.

title: Mobile-side ChannelTransport (Android)
description:
New module in letta-mobile core/src/main/java/com/letta/mobile/data/channel/:

- ChannelTransport.kt: WS connect, hello, frame send/recv loop, foreground-only lifecycle
- ChannelProtocol.kt: frame data classes (kotlinx.serialization)
- ChannelConfig.kt: settings keys for url, token, device_id (generated UUID, persisted)
- ChannelChatSender.kt: send_message + collect frames as Flow<UiMessage>

Wire AdminChatViewModel (or TimelineSendCoordinator) to consult a setting 'chat.transport' = rest|channel. Default rest. When channel: route sends via ChannelChatSender. Admin (conv list, blocks, models) stays on REST.

Foreground-only: connect on chat screen open, disconnect on close. No reconnect logic; user reopens app on drop.

Mirror docs/MOBILE_CHANNEL_DESIGN.md Phase 1 vocabulary exactly.

Acceptance: settings toggle on → chat works identically to REST path; toggle off → falls back; no UI regressions.
notes: Mirror bead filed in the letta-mobile project as letta-mobile-jpg8. Coordinate landing order: server-side (lcp-gj2.1 → .4) lands first, this depends on those.

title: Phase 1 protocol test harness
description:
Standalone node script (~/.letta/channels/mobile/test/ws-smoke.mjs) that:

1. Connects to ws://localhost:8291/shim/v1/mobile
2. Sends hello with the dev token
3. Sends send_message to Meridian's default conv
4. Collects frames until stop_reason
5. Asserts frame order, types, content non-empty, [DONE] semantics if applicable
6. Times the round-trip
7. Exits 0 on success, 1 on shape mismatch

Acceptance: 'node ws-smoke.mjs' passes against the running shim.

title: Wire WS upgrade into admin-shim
description:
admin-shim/server.mjs accepts WS upgrades on /shim/v1/mobile and hands the socket to the mobile channel plugin's acceptConnection method.

- Add 'ws' dep to admin-shim/package.json (or lib/, document in DIVERGENCE.md)
- Wire createServer's 'upgrade' event to a router
- Route /shim/v1/mobile to the plugin
- All other paths (/v1/*, /shim/pool, etc.) keep working unchanged

Acceptance: curl --include --no-buffer --http1.1 --header 'Upgrade: websocket' ... shows 101 Switching Protocols on /shim/v1/mobile; 404 on unknown WS paths.

title: send_message → worker pool integration
description:
Mobile channel adapter's send_message handler calls getAgentPool().get(convId, agentId), writes the user message JSON line to worker stdin (reusing chat.mjs's existing logic), and streams reply frames back over WS in vanilla order: turn_started → assistant_message (coalesced) → stop_reason → usage_statistics.

Reuse reshapeFrame + coalesce logic verbatim from admin-shim/lib/chat.mjs. The pool is shared between REST and channel transports.

Acceptance: a node test script opens WS, sends hello + send_message, receives the full ordered frame sequence and a coalesced single assistant_message.

title: Channel adapter scaffold for mobile
description:
Create ~/.letta/channels/mobile/ with channel.json, plugin.mjs entry, and lib/ scaffolding mirroring the Matrix plugin structure.

Files:
- channel.json: id=mobile, displayName='Letta Mobile', entry='./plugin.mjs', runtimePackages: ['ws@8.x']
- plugin.mjs: thin entry; exports channelPlugin metadata + createAdapter
- lib/ws-handler.mjs: accept WS upgrade, parse frames, dispatch
- lib/protocol.mjs: frame definitions per Phase 1 vocabulary (hello, welcome, send_message, turn_started, assistant_message, stop_reason, etc.)
- accounts.json: single account with hard-coded MOBILE_CHANNEL_TOKEN env var

Acceptance: 'letta channels status' shows 'mobile' as configured.

title: Epic: Mobile-as-channel — replace REST chat with channel pipeline
description:
Make letta-mobile a first-class channel like Matrix/Slack. Mobile's chat path moves from the REST/SSE shim onto a WebSocket riding letta-code's channel pipeline. Admin stays on REST. See docs/MOBILE_CHANNEL_DESIGN.md for the full design.

Five phases:
  Phase 1: minimum viable WS round-trip (hard-coded token, one conv)
  Phase 2: pairing flow, multi-conv routing, sync cursor + reconnect
  Phase 3: server-pushed lifecycle events (typing, reasoning, tool calls,
           agent-initiated messages)
  Phase 4: push notifications via UnifiedPush (FCM optional), gated on
           Phase 2 cursor + Phase 3 taxonomy
  Phase 5: multi-device fan-out

Each phase shippable on its own. Mobile gets a 'use channel transport for
chat' toggle once Phase 1 lands; flip on/off per device.

Architectural contract: shim hosts both REST and WS on the same port.
Channel plugin lives at ~/.letta/channels/mobile/. Worker pool is shared
between REST and channel — warm workers serve either transport. /v1/* stays
strictly vanilla-shaped (per docs/admin-shim/DIVERGENCE.md); the WS
endpoint lives under /shim/v1/.

title: Remote action dispatch: tap, scroll, text input from CLI
description:
Third slice. CLI can drive the app — tap a component by ID, scroll a list, type into a field. Closes the loop from observation to interaction.

## Wire shape (proposed)

```json
{
  "type": "ui_introspect",
  "op": "action",
  "request_id": "...",
  "action": {
    "kind": "tap" | "long_press" | "scroll" | "text_input" | "key",
    "target_id": "send-btn",
    "params": { "text": "hello", "dx": 0, "dy": -200 }
  }
}
```

Response includes the post-action snapshot so CLI doesn't need to follow up.

## Design

- Target by stable component ID (from snapshot/subscribe), NOT by screen coordinates — robust against layout shifts
- Use Compose's testTag + SemanticsActions where possible (onClick, scrollBy, setText)
- Fall back to coordinate-based dispatch only when the component has no semantic action
- Permission gate: actions require an explicit `--allow-drive` flag on the CLI side; shim refuses unconfirmed action frames from unknown CLI connections
- Audit: every action logged with request_id, device_id, CLI session id

## Risk

This is the dangerous one. Lets a remote CLI tap arbitrary buttons on a running phone. Auth/scope MUST be tight before this lands. Specifically:

- Bearer token must be the same scoped token the CLI used for snapshot/subscribe
- Probably gate behind a developer-mode flag on the device (not on by default in user builds)
- Confirm with Emmanuel before exposing in any non-dev build

## Acceptance

- `letta ui tap <id>`, `letta ui type <id> '<text>'`, `letta ui scroll <id> --dy -200` all work
- Actions are reflected in the next snapshot
- Dev-mode gate on the device prevents drive in non-dev builds
- Audit log retained on shim for debugging

title: Live tree subscription: stream deltas on recomposition
description:
Second slice. CLI subscribes; app streams ASCII tree deltas on each meaningful recomposition.

## Wire shape (proposed)

Subscribe:
```json
{ "type": "ui_introspect", "op": "subscribe", "subscription_id": "...", "throttle_ms": 100 }
```

Delta frames (server-initiated after subscribe):
```json
{
  "type": "ui_introspect_delta",
  "subscription_id": "...",
  "seq": 17,
  "screen_id": "ChatScreen",
  "changed": [{ "id": "send-btn", "state": ["disabled", "loading"] }],
  "full_tree": null
}
```

Unsubscribe:
```json
{ "type": "ui_introspect", "op": "unsubscribe", "subscription_id": "..." }
```

## Design

- Diff against last-sent snapshot; send full tree on screen change, deltas otherwise
- Throttle on the device side (default 100ms) to avoid flooding on heavy recomp
- Single subscription per CLI connection initially — fan-out is a later optimization
- Coalesce rapid changes within the throttle window

## Acceptance

- `letta ui watch [--device <id>]` streams live ASCII to terminal, repainting in place
- Subscription survives screen transitions (sends new full tree on screen_id change)
- Disconnect cleans up server-side subscription state
- Throttling prevents runaway frame rates during animations

title: Read-only ASCII snapshot: app→shim→CLI
description:
First slice. CLI requests current screen, app returns ASCII projection of the active Compose tree, shim relays.

## Wire shape (proposed)

CLI → shim → device:
```json
{ "type": "ui_introspect", "op": "snapshot", "request_id": "..." }
```

Device → shim → CLI:
```json
{
  "type": "ui_introspect_response",
  "request_id": "...",
  "screen_id": "ChatScreen",
  "tree": "ascii string",
  "components": [{ "id": "send-btn", "bounds": [120, 400, 200, 440], "state": ["enabled"] }]
}
```

## ASCII format requirements

- Window frame with screen title
- Component boundaries labeled (Card, Column, List, Button, Text, etc.)
- State annotations inline ([disabled], [loading], [selected])
- Live dimensions (list item counts, tab counts)
- Stable IDs so the renderer/agent can reference 'the send button in ChatScreen' deterministically

## Implementation notes

- Generated from the live Compose tree via SemanticsNode walk (not source analysis — would lose runtime state)
- Probably under SemanticsOwner.rootSemanticsNode or LocalView.current.semanticsOwner
- Read-only: NO side effects on the app

## Acceptance

- CLI command: `letta ui snapshot [--device <id>]` returns ASCII to stdout
- shim relays the request to the targeted device's WS connection
- App returns within 500ms on a quiet screen
- ASCII fits within a normal terminal width (80-120 cols) at the top level; deeper trees indent

title: ASCII UI introspection: remote-drive mobile app from CLI over shim WS
description:
Live ASCII projection of the Android Compose UI, surfaced through the admin-shim WS, driven from the new lcp CLI.

## Motivation

Meridian (and any agent reasoning about the mobile UI) currently has to infer screen state from source code. That's brittle and stale within a day. A live ASCII projection of the current Compose tree would let agents and humans reason deliberately about what the user actually sees before emitting A2UI surfaces or making layout changes.

## Architecture

- **Driver service** lives in admin-shim (already terminates mobile WS, has auth, sees all devices)
- **CLI binary** lives in letta-code-parallel (new CLI being built; right home for ad-hoc dev tooling)
- **Device hook** lives in letta-mobile android-compose, surfaced over the existing /shim/v1/mobile WS contract
- **Wire format** extends the WS protocol with ui_introspect envelope (subtypes: snapshot, action, subscribe)

Shim is the multiplexer — CLI dials shim, shim relays to the chosen device.

## Scope (split into sub-tickets)

1. Read-only ASCII snapshot (request/response, no streaming)
2. Subscription / live delta stream on recomposition
3. Remote action dispatch (tap, scroll, text input) for interactive driving

## Not in scope (yet)

- Multi-device fan-out beyond simple device picker
- Desktop host support (will reuse same protocol when Desktop shell lands)
- Cross-workspace device discovery

title: mobile ws-handler: replace 120s no-traffic close with WS-protocol ping/pong liveness
description:
home/.letta/channels/mobile/lib/ws-handler.mjs has a 120-second no-inbound-traffic timer that closes the socket with code 1000, reason='idle timeout' (lines 84-90). resetIdle() only fires on inbound client messages (line 317), so any time the user is reading rather than typing, the timer ticks down and the socket is killed.

This is wrong for the canonical live transport. Per the transport-exclusivity contract that landed 2026-05-25 (admin-shim advertises canonical_live_transport=ws in welcome frame, per letta_connection_contract.md §'Transport-mode exclusivity'), WS is the only live mutator path for owned conversations. Killing it every 2 minutes of read-time defeats the contract.

Observed live tonight: 13-minute idle gap (22:32 -> 22:45 EDT) while Emmanuel was reading the previous reply, no client traffic, server-side timer fired, socket closed, mobile app surfaced 'idle timeout' as a user-visible toast (companion bug — see letta-mobile ticket filed in same session).

## Fix

Replace the no-traffic timer with WebSocket-protocol ping/pong:

1. Server sends ws.ping() every ~30s
2. Server tracks last received pong
3. If no pong arrives within ~90s (3 ping intervals), close with code 1011 (server error) and reason 'no pong'
4. resetIdle() goes away entirely; lastPongAt is the only liveness signal

Env tunables (suggest):
- SHIM_MOBILE_WS_PING_MS — default 30000
- SHIM_MOBILE_WS_PONG_DEADLINE_MS — default 90000

Both 'ping' send and pong-deadline timers use unref() so they don't hold the process open.

## Why ping/pong, not app-level

- WS protocol ping/pong is wire-level, RFC 6455 §5.5.2 defined exactly for this
- Costs <10 bytes per 30s, negligible battery
- Faster dead-socket detection than TCP keepalive (which defaults to 2+ hours on Linux)
- Standard pattern; production WS servers do this
- Decouples 'is the socket alive' from 'is the user actively typing' — they're different questions

## Why NOT just drop the timer (option 1 from the discussion)

Agent-pool's 300s idle-evict is about RESOURCE lifetime, not SOCKET liveness. They measure different things. Pushing socket liveness to TCP keepalive means waiting hours to detect a dead socket, which interacts badly with letta-mobile-mvon-class bugs (stale WS, silent action drops).

## Out of scope for this ticket

- Mobile-side toast suppression — filed separately in letta-mobile rig (companion ticket)
- Reconnect cursor / resume semantics — already covered by background-mode resume from letta_connection_contract.md

## References

- $MEMORY_DIR/system/letta_connection_contract.md §'Transport-mode exclusivity — wire-level contract'
- $MEMORY_DIR/system/letta_cloud_unification.md §'Mobile + streaming' (intermittent-by-default design)
- ws-handler.mjs:69, :84-90, :114-115 (existing comments acknowledging the dual-clock concern)
- letta-mobile companion ticket (filed same session 2026-05-25)
acceptance_criteria:
1. ws-handler.mjs no longer has a no-traffic 'idle timeout' close path.
2. Server sends ws.ping() at SHIM_MOBILE_WS_PING_MS (default 30s) cadence while the socket is open and past hello.
3. Pong handler updates lastPongAt; deadline timer closes the socket with code 1011 (or 1000, see decision) and a diagnostic reason string if no pong within SHIM_MOBILE_WS_PONG_DEADLINE_MS (default 90s).
4. Reading-only client (no client→server frames for 10+ minutes) keeps the socket open as long as pongs respond.
5. Force-killing the client (kill -9 the app, airplane mode the device) results in socket closure within PONG_DEADLINE_MS, not 2+ hours.
6. Tests: ws-protocol.test.ts gains a 'long read-idle keeps WS alive via ping/pong' case and a 'no pong → close within deadline' case.

title: Tool returns surface at end-of-turn instead of per-tool — incremental disk-watch enhancement
description:
# Tool returns synthesized at end-of-turn instead of per-tool — incremental disk-watch enhancement

## Summary

The lcp-4vz fix that landed in mobile-channel-host.ts works (tool returns now appear, cards reach completion) but synthesizes ALL missing tool_return_message frames in a single batch AFTER `pool.runTurnWithHeal` returns. From the user's perspective, tool cards stay in their "Running" state for the entire turn duration and then all flip to "completed" together when the run ends.

Per-tool real-time progression is the desired behavior. The disk has the result available within milliseconds of each tool's execution finishing, so the data is there to surface — the shim just isn't watching for it incrementally.

## Why end-of-turn batching is the current behavior

Trace from a verified-fixed probe (2026-05-24 ~18:30 EDT):

The CLI emits these wire events in order during a 3-tool turn:
1. approval_request_message (call #1)
2. auto_approval (SDK drops it — invisible to shim adapter)
3. ... CLI executes tool internally ...
4. approval_request_message (call #2)
5. auto_approval (dropped)
6. ... and so on

The SDK pump only forwards events it recognizes — `auto_approval` is not one of them, so the shim adapter never sees a per-tool "this one just finished" signal. The shim's only choice with the current architecture is to wait for the turn to end and diff the disk.

## Scaling concerns (Emmanuel raised, valid)

A naive "one fs.watch per active turn" would not scale:
- Linux inotify cap (`fs.inotify.max_user_watches`, default 8192) is exhaustible
- File watch fires on every CLI write (assistant deltas, not just tool returns)
- Each event would trigger full re-parse of messages.jsonl, which grows unboundedly per conversation
- N concurrent turns → N watchers + N parses

## Design constraints any fix must satisfy

1. **One watcher per `agent_id::conversation_id`, NOT per turn.** Refcounted, shared across concurrent connections to the same conv. Most rigs have ≤1 active turn per conv at a time.

2. **Track read offset; only parse new bytes.** Stat the file for size, seek from last offset, parse only the suffix. Conv files are append-only, so this is O(new bytes), not O(file size).

3. **In-memory turn state**, not per-event computation. `Map<runId, {pendingCallIds: Set, resolvedCallIds: Set}>`. The watcher's only job: "new bytes appeared, parse them, emit any new tool_return frames whose call_id matches a pending entry".

4. **Idle teardown.** Close the watcher when no active turns reference the conv, after a short idle window (5-10s). Mirror the agent pool's existing housekeep loop pattern (SHIM_POOL_IDLE_SEC).

5. **Debounce write events.** Coalesce file events with a small debounce (~50ms). Tool returns aren't latency-critical sub-100ms; UI smoothness wins over per-byte freshness.

6. **Bounded re-read.** Cap parse work at last N bytes or N entries — tool returns are at the tail of the file. Never re-walk the whole file from byte 0.

7. **Graceful fallback to end-of-turn synthesis.** If the watcher fails to start (e.g. inotify exhaustion, file not yet created), the existing end-of-turn batch path remains as the safety net. Don't regress to "no frames" if the optimization fails.

## Suggested implementation shape

```ts
// Per-conversation watcher state, shared across turns
const convWatchers = new Map<string, {
  watcher: FSWatcher,
  offset: number,           // last parsed byte offset
  refCount: number,         // active turns on this conv
  pendingTurns: Map<string, { pendingCallIds: Set<string>, resolvedCallIds: Set<string> }>,
  idleTimer: NodeJS.Timeout | null,
  emitFns: Set<(frame: BridgeFrame) => void>,
}>();

function attachToolReturnWatcher(convKey, runId, onFrame, pendingCallIds) {
  let w = convWatchers.get(convKey);
  if (!w) {
    w = createWatcher(convKey);   // fs.watch + debounce + offset
    convWatchers.set(convKey, w);
  }
  w.refCount++;
  w.pendingTurns.set(runId, { pendingCallIds, resolvedCallIds: new Set() });
  w.emitFns.add(onFrame);
  // Return detach handle for end-of-turn cleanup
  return () => {
    w.refCount--;
    w.pendingTurns.delete(runId);
    w.emitFns.delete(onFrame);
    if (w.refCount === 0) {
      scheduleIdleClose(w, 10_000);
    }
  };
}
```

End-of-turn synthesis (the current code) stays as the closing-the-gap pass for any tool_call that the watcher missed (race, fallback, etc).

## Expected user-visible behavior after fix

Today: 3 bash calls → cards spin → all 3 flip to checkmark when run completes (1-30s after the last tool finished).

After fix: 3 bash calls → each card flips to checkmark within ~50-100ms of its own tool completing → next assistant text streams in normally.

## Files involved

- `admin-shim/lib/mobile-channel-host.ts` — currently owns the end-of-turn synthesis. New per-conv watcher infra lives here (or in a sibling `tool-return-watcher.ts` if it grows).
- `admin-shim/lib/store.ts` — `listMessages` is the current disk-read API. New watcher needs a lower-level "read suffix from offset" primitive; can add to store.ts.
- `admin-shim/lib/agent-pool.ts` — housekeep loop is the reference pattern for idle teardown.

## Honesty footer

- "~50-100ms latency" is an estimate based on fs.watch typical latency + debounce window; not benchmarked.
- The "one watcher per conv" assumption assumes conv = (agent_id, conversation_id). If the rig ever supports N concurrent runs on the SAME conv (e.g. parallel approval runs per letta_connection_contract.md Q4), the in-memory turn state map already handles it correctly — but each turn still shares the conv's single watcher.
- inotify is Linux-specific. macOS uses FSEvents and Windows uses ReadDirectoryChangesW; node's fs.watch abstracts them but has known platform quirks. Shim runs on Linux (Debian/Ubuntu) so this is fine in practice, but document the assumption.
- I did NOT verify the inotify default cap on the current host. `cat /proc/sys/fs/inotify/max_user_watches` will show it.

## Cross-references

- lcp-4vz — parent bug. End-of-turn synthesis is the v1 fix; this is the v2 enhancement.
- lcp-8ri — stop_reason=requires_approval mismatch. Still open. Separate fix; not addressed here.
- lcp-wqy — Jan-1 timestamp leak. Still open. Separate fix; not addressed here.
- letta_connection_contract.md memory — preserves "ordered stream events" rule. Per-tool incremental delivery improves ordering granularity even if end-of-turn batching is technically still ordered.
