- admin-shim/test/ws-protocol.test.ts (extend): hello → cron_add → cron_list returns the task → cron_get returns it → cron_delete → cron_list empty. Second client sees crons_updated push.
- admin-shim/test/crons-store.test.ts (new): addTask field round-trip; concurrent addTask serialization (two withLock callers); stale-lock theft (mkdir + sleep + reclaim with dead pid in owner.json); 50-per-agent cap; deleteAllTasks scoping.
- admin-shim/test/cron-scheduler.test.ts (new): fake-time tick with a '* * * * *' task fires exactly once and calls handleSendMessage with wrapped envelope; one-shot fires + status→fired; late one-shot → missed; recurring fire_count++; lease conflict refuses second scheduler; SIGTERM releases lease.
- admin-shim/test/crons-rest.test.ts (new): GET /v1/crons returns parity with WS cron_list; GET /v1/crons/scheduler shape; POST returns 405.
- mtime-watch integration test (in cron-scheduler.test.ts): write crons.json externally, assert tasks_active reflects within 1s + crons_updated emitted.
acceptance_criteria:
- All test files run green under 'npm test'.
- No test depends on real wall-clock — use fake timers (node:test mock or Sinon-equivalent if added).
- Tests cover at minimum: CRUD round-trip, lock contention, lease conflict, fire path with envelope, missed-window, mtime-watch.
- Tests run in <30s on the workstation.

title: lcp-d5g.2: WS cron frames in mobile channel (cron_add/list/get/delete + crons_updated)
description:
Mirror Letta Cloud's WS cron protocol on the mobile channel so the app can CRUD scheduled tasks over the existing WebSocket without holding a second connection or hitting REST for writes.

# What to build
- home/.letta/channels/mobile/lib/protocol.mjs: parse + validate inbound cron_list, cron_add, cron_get, cron_delete, cron_delete_all; serialize outbound cron_list_response, cron_add_response, cron_get_response, cron_delete_response, cron_delete_all_response, crons_updated.
- home/.letta/channels/mobile/lib/ws-handler.mjs: route these frames to host handlers, enforce MOBILE_CHANNEL_TOKEN (already in place for other frames).
- admin-shim/lib/mobile-channel-host.ts: handleCronList / handleCronAdd / handleCronGet / handleCronDelete / handleCronDeleteAll, all backed by lcp-d5g.1's crons.ts. Run inbound agent_id through resolveAgentIdAlias before touching the store.
- On any mutation (add/delete/delete_all), broadcast crons_updated to all connected mobile sockets that are subscribed to the affected agent_id (or all, if scope=null).
- Frame shapes mirror Letta Cloud verbatim: { type, request_id?, agent_id?, conversation_id?, task?, tasks?, success, error?, warning? }.

# Why
- Per the saved memory shim-new-features-mutations-ws-reads-may-mirror-rest, all net-new mutations go over WS. Mirroring Letta Cloud's frame names lets us share a single protocol with the upstream mobile app's existing schedules tab.

# Notes
- Requires letta-code's scheduler-lease format on add — surface the bundle's 'No letta server is currently running' warning as our shim's 'scheduler not yet started' when applicable (should rarely trigger once lcp-d5g.3 lands).
acceptance_criteria:
- Mobile WS round-trip: hello → cron_add → cron_list shows it → cron_delete → cron_list empty.
- A second connected client receives crons_updated within 100ms of a peer's cron_add.
- cron_add with an invalid cron expression returns success=false with error and does NOT persist.
- Inbound agent_id aliases resolve to the canonical agent-id in the persisted task.
- Auth: a connection without a valid MOBILE_CHANNEL_TOKEN is rejected before any cron frame is processed.

title: lcp-d5g.1: Shim-side crons.ts store (lock-aware CRUD on crons.json)
description:
Port letta-code's crons.json read/write logic into admin-shim/lib/crons.ts so the shim can manage scheduled tasks without shelling out to 'letta cron'. This is the storage primitive everything else (WS protocol, scheduler, REST mirror) depends on.

# What to build
- admin-shim/lib/crons.ts exporting: readCronFile, writeCronFile (atomic via .tmp+rename), addTask, listTasks(filters), getTask, deleteTask, deleteAllTasks(agentId).
- Lock helpers: acquireLock (mkdir-based on $LETTA_HOME/crons.lock with owner.json), withLock(fn). Port LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS=5000, LOCK_RETRY_MS=50, LOCK_STALE_AGE_MS=30000, captureProcessIdentity (pid + process_start_ticks + boot_id) so we interoperate with the existing letta-code skill that may also write the file.
- Port helpers: parseEvery (5m/2h/1d → cron), parseAt (3pm / in 45m → scheduled_for), isValidCron, computeJitter.
- Limits as env-configurable: SHIM_CRON_MAX_ACTIVE_PER_AGENT (default 50), SHIM_CRON_MISSED_THRESHOLD_MS (default 5*60_000).
- TS types in admin-shim/lib/types/crons.ts: CronTask, CronFile, SchedulerOwner, LockOwner — match crons.json shape verbatim so the file remains compatible with letta-code.

# Why
- Avoids shell-out overhead and lets us add WS frames + REST without process spawn per call.
- Keeps full compatibility with the on-disk format so the bundled letta skill can still self-schedule and we pick it up.
- Sets us up to choose our own limits without forking the bundle.
acceptance_criteria:
- Round-trip a task through addTask → readCronFile → getTask with all 19 fields preserved.
- Two processes contending for addTask serialize cleanly via the lock (test).
- A stale lock (>30s + dead PID) is stolen rather than blocking.
- listTasks honors agent_id + conversation_id filters.
- deleteAllTasks(agentId) removes only that agent's rows and reports the count.

title: Epic: Scheduled prompts (cron) via mobile WS + read-only REST
description:
Expose letta-code's cron scheduling capability through the admin-shim so mobile clients (and ad-hoc observers) can schedule recurring/one-shot prompts at agents without depending on Letta Cloud or a separately-running 'letta server' listener.

# Why this exists
- letta-code ships a cron feature (letta cron add/list/delete) backed by $LETTA_HOME/crons.json under a mkdir-lock. The doc + bundle source confirm tasks only FIRE while something holds the scheduler lease — that 'something' is normally 'letta server', which our shim deliberately does NOT run (to stay independent of Letta Cloud's agent-count cap and other limits).
- Mobile clients today have no way to schedule prompts. We need to fill that gap while preserving our 'shim is the sole writer' architecture.

# Scope
- Mutations (add/get/list/delete/delete-all) are exposed over the existing mobile WS channel (/shim/v1/mobile), mirroring Letta Cloud's frame style (cron_add / cron_list / *_response / crons_updated push). MOBILE_CHANNEL_TOKEN auth.
- Read-only mirror is also exposed under REST /v1/crons* and /v1/crons/scheduler for passive observers (dashboards, curl, monitoring).
- Shim runs the scheduler itself: claim the lease, 60s tick, fire by wrapping the prompt in <system-reminder> envelope and calling handleSendMessage via the existing agent-pool. No second daemon.
- We pick our own limits (port the 50/agent + 5-min-missed defaults but make them env-configurable).
- Agent self-scheduling via the bundled letta skill keeps working — skill shells out to 'letta cron add' which writes our local crons.json; our scheduler picks it up on the next tick (mtime watch triggers a crons_updated push).

# Out of scope
- Registering as a Letta Cloud device (deliberately avoided — would re-couple us to Cloud's agent cap).
- Multi-listener scheduler election beyond the single existing lease primitive.

# Children
Tracked via dependencies on this epic.
design: See conversation in /opt/stacks/letta-code-parallel session (2026-05-18). Key decisions: WS-first for mutations (per shim-new-features-mutations-ws-reads-may-mirror-rest memory), REST mirror for reads only, scheduler runs in-shim (option B from research, not co-located letta server), no Cloud device registration.
acceptance_criteria:
- Mobile client can add a recurring task over WS and see it fire at the agent within one tick of its cron time.
- Mobile client can add a one-shot --at task and see it fire then transition to 'fired'.
- Late one-shot tasks (>5min) transition to 'missed' without firing.
- agent self-schedule via the letta skill is reflected in GET /v1/crons within the next tick (mtime watch) and emits a crons_updated push to subscribed mobile clients.
- Shutting down the shim releases the scheduler lease cleanly so a restart can claim it.
- All firing flows through agent-pool, never a second 'letta server' process.
- README + MOBILE_WS_PROTOCOL.md document the new frames + REST routes.
close_reason: All 6 children closed — store + WS + scheduler + REST + tests + docs all shipped on 2026-05-19

title: A2UI: top-level message arrays inside <a2ui-json> are a Letta convention, not in upstream spec
description:
Our embedded prompt template (admin-shim/lib/a2ui-v09-basic-prompt.ts: 'a single, raw JSON object (usually a list of A2UI messages)') and validator (a2ui-stream-splitter.ts:200-207 — validateA2uiMessage recurses into arrays) both accept top-level arrays of A2UI messages inside a single <a2ui-json> block.

But the upstream v0.9 server_to_client.json schema is oneOf of four single-message variants (createSurface | updateComponents | updateDataModel | deleteSurface). There is no array-of-messages shape in the spec. A stock A2UI validator handed our batched output would reject it.

This is the most subtle interop hazard we have: any third-party A2UI tooling pointed at our wire will see invalid envelopes.

Fix options:

(a) Drop array support. validateA2uiMessage rejects top-level arrays. Prompt-template language is updated to 'a single A2UI message'. If the model needs to emit multiple messages (e.g. createSurface + updateComponents), it emits multiple <a2ui-json> blocks back-to-back — the splitter already supports it cleanly.

(b) Keep array support; document the batched-array as a Letta extension. Add a comment to a2ui-stream-splitter.ts and a section to MOBILE_WS_PROTOCOL.md. Accept interop tax.

Recommendation: (a). Tighter spec compliance, no expressive loss (multiple blocks work), removes a category of fan-out confusion in a2ui_frame emission (one frame in = one frame out).
close_reason: Aligned A2UI blocks with upstream v0.9 single-message envelopes: validator rejects top-level arrays, prompt/docs instruct multiple adjacent blocks, tests updated.

title: A2UI sendDataModel:true has no wire path — form values are lost on submit
description:
A2UI v0.9 surface-to-server data flow: when createSurface includes sendDataModel:true, the client is contractually required to attach a2uiClientDataModel (full surface state) to every user message metadata.

Currently broken in two places:

1. The shim's user_action frame contract (admin-shim/docs/MOBILE_WS_PROTOCOL.md §2.1; mobile-channel-host.ts handleUserAction) has no field for a client data model. There is no metadata envelope.

2. Even if we add the field, the recording-only contract noted in beads memory (a2ui-phase-5-user-action-is-a-recording) means the agent side currently doesn't consume user_action at all.

Real impact: if a model emits a Form with TextField/ChoicePicker inputs and createSurface{ sendDataModel: true }, the user fills it in, clicks Submit (Button with action.event), the form values are dropped on the floor. The agent receives an event name but no field data.

Fix options:

(a) Wire it end to end. Add data_model: JsonObject? to user_action frame schema. Shim ingests, strips into Letta tool dispatcher context. Requires phase 5b sibling work (lcp-uo5.8 wire user_action to tool dispatcher gate) to be done first or in parallel.

(b) Forbid sendDataModel:true in our v0.9 subset for now. Validator rejects createSurface where sendDataModel===true. Prompt is instructed to never emit it. Defers the question, breaks Form workflows.

Recommendation: (a) but as a dedicated phase. Depends on lcp-uo5.8 landing. Currently we ship Forms that look interactive but silently fail — that's the user-facing bug worth tracking, even if the fix is later.
close_reason: Chose safe option (b): createSurface.sendDataModel=true is rejected and documented until lcp-uo5.8 provides true dispatcher delivery, eliminating silent form data loss.

title: A2UI theme_hints accepted in negotiation but never injected into model prompt
description:
negotiateA2uiCapability (admin-shim/lib/a2ui-adapter.ts:70-83) validates and captures the client's theme_hints into A2uiCapability.themeHints, but buildA2uiSystemPrompt (a2ui-adapter.ts:105-121) never references it.

Result: mobile sends { color_scheme: 'dark' } in the hello frame → server logs negotiation success → model has no idea about the client's theme → every emitted createSurface uses default styling.

A2UI v0.9 supports theme on createSurface via the catalog's theme schema (primaryColor: hex regex, iconUrl, agentDisplayName, plus additionalProperties for extensions like color_scheme).

Fix options:

(a) Inject themeHints into the prompt augmentation block. Tell the model: 'When emitting createSurface, set the theme field to: {…serialized themeHints…}'. Renderer-side, the theme primaryColor must match ^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$, so we should pre-validate the hint shape before forwarding.

(b) Drop the field from negotiation and document theme_hints as reserved for future use. Stop accepting the field on the wire so the API surface honestly reflects current behavior.

Recommendation: (a) — it's the smaller diff and unblocks a real product capability (dark-mode UIs). Constrain primaryColor to upstream regex; for color_scheme ('light'/'dark'/'system'), include as a free-form prompt hint.
close_reason: Injected sanitized theme_hints into the A2UI system prompt and covered valid/invalid primaryColor behavior with tests.

title: A2UI capability negotiation: negative test coverage (disabled / version-mismatch / catalog-mismatch / opt-out)
description:
A2UI capability handshake regression test.

The lcp-uo5.2 commits documented A2UI negotiation knobs and added the hello-handshake response carrying a2ui_negotiated + a2ui (version/catalog summary). There is one positive test (ws: hello can negotiate A2UI capability when server support is enabled) but no negative tests exercising the actual gates.

Missing coverage:
- A2UI_ENABLED=0: hello must reply a2ui_negotiated=false even when client requests it.
- Version mismatch: client requests version 0.10, server only supports 0.9, must reply a2ui_negotiated=false with a clear reason.
- Catalog mismatch: client requests an unknown catalog id, must reply a2ui_negotiated=false.
- Client never requests A2UI in hello: server must NOT inject A2UI schema into the system prompt even if A2UI_ENABLED=1 globally.
- Stale negotiation: subsequent send_message frames on a session that did NOT negotiate A2UI must reject any inbound a2ui_frame attempts.

Without these tests, a future change to the negotiation logic can silently leak A2UI behavior into non-A2UI sessions (wasting tokens on schema injection, surfacing frames to clients that cannot render them) or silently disable A2UI for clients that should have it.

Non-goals: end-to-end render tests, multi-version coexistence, client-side capability validation.

Rollback: if a test surfaces a real negotiation bug, fix the negotiation rather than relax the test.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Test: A2UI_ENABLED=0 returns a2ui_negotiated=false in hello reply even when client requests A2UI.
2. Test: client requesting an unsupported A2UI version returns a2ui_negotiated=false with a documented reason field.
3. Test: client requesting an unsupported catalog id returns a2ui_negotiated=false.
4. Test: client that does NOT request A2UI gets no schema injection (assertable via the system prompt length or a sentinel marker).
5. Test: inbound a2ui_frame or user_action on a session that did not negotiate A2UI is rejected with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
6. All five tests run in the existing ws-protocol.test.ts file or a sibling a2ui-negotiation.test.ts and pass on master plus on a fresh feature branch.
close_reason: Added negative negotiation coverage for disabled/version mismatch/catalog mismatch/opt-out and rejected stale inbound A2UI frames; handler now reports rejection reasons.

title: A2UI splitter: property-based / fuzz tests for adversarial model output
description:
A2UI splitter property-based test coverage.

The stream splitter (admin-shim/lib/a2ui-stream-splitter.ts, 252 lines) is the parser between conversational text and structured frames. It runs against adversarial model output (tags split across chunks, malformed JSON, nested tags, missing closes, embedded HTML-looking content) and never throws. Today it has 192 lines of unit tests covering the happy path plus a handful of edge cases.

For a splitter that runs against an adversarial input source (the model), unit tests alone are not enough. We need property-based fuzzing that asserts the splitter invariants for any input: (a) never throws, (b) total text bytes emitted plus total raw bytes captured equals input minus tag delimiters, (c) no captured block can straddle a tag boundary, (d) malformed JSON is always reported as a block with ok=false, never silently dropped.

This bead adds a fuzz suite. Approach: generate inputs via a small grammar (text chunks, opens, closes, partial opens/closes, broken JSON, valid JSON) and feed them to the splitter in random groupings of 1-100 char deltas. Run 10000 iterations. Any invariant break = test failure with the seed dumped.

Non-goals: full coverage-guided fuzzing (no AFL), JSON schema validation (separate concern in the validator), runtime stats.

Rollback: if fuzzing surfaces a real bug, fix the splitter rather than weaken the invariant.
acceptance_criteria:
1. New test file a2ui-stream-splitter.fuzz.test.ts runs >=10000 randomized cases against a small grammar of text+tag inputs.
2. Invariants asserted on every case: never-throws, no-text-bytes-lost, blocks-never-straddle-tags, malformed-JSON-surfaces-as-ok=false.
3. On failure, the seed and reproducing input are dumped so the case is replayable.
4. Suite completes in under 5 seconds locally; documented in the test header so CI budget is predictable.
5. A regression: feeding a known-bad input from a real model trace (captured as a fixture under test/fixtures/a2ui-adversarial/) passes.
6. The non-fuzz test suite continues to pass unchanged.
close_reason: Added deterministic 10k-case A2UI splitter fuzz suite plus adversarial fixture, covering never-throw and parser preservation invariants.

title: A2UI observability: per-turn metrics + parse/validate failure logging
description:
A2UI surface observability gap.

The shim now parses, validates, and forwards a2ui_frame messages but emits no metrics. After ship we will need to answer: how many frames per turn, what fraction parse-fail, what fraction validate-fail, latency from upstream chunk arrival to a2ui_frame emission, count of unknown widgets seen in the wild.

Without these numbers we cannot detect renderer-side regressions (validator passing frames the renderer refuses), prompt drift (catalogs that worked stop working), or unbounded growth (a runaway turn emitting hundreds of frames).

Current: a2ui-stream-splitter has no instrumentation hooks. Frame validation in a2ui-stream-splitter and downstream rejection in mobile-channel-host happen silently.

Desired: structured logger emits per-turn metrics with run_id, agent_id, total_frames, parse_ok, parse_err, validate_ok, validate_err, widget_types_seen, splitter_overhead_ms, plus inline warn-level logs for parse/validate failures with the offending raw block snippet truncated to 200 chars.

Minimal hookpoint: a single onMetrics callback on the splitter constructor, fed from mobile-channel-host into a structured logger that already exists in the shim.

Non-goals: Prometheus, dashboards, sampling. Just logs we can grep.

Rollback signal: if the logger is too chatty (more than 1 line per 100 model tokens), reduce verbosity rather than remove.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Structured log line per turn includes run_id, agent_id, total_frames, parse_ok/err counts, validate_ok/err counts, widget_types_seen (deduped), splitter_overhead_ms.
2. Parse failures emit a warn-level log with the offending raw block truncated to 200 chars and the parse error message.
3. Validation failures emit a warn-level log with the widget type, validation error, and a truncated raw block.
4. Splitter exposes an onMetrics(callback) constructor option that fires at end-of-turn.
5. Verbosity bound: at most 1 log line per 100 model tokens under normal traffic; configurable via A2UI_METRICS_VERBOSITY.
6. A test asserts the log line schema is stable (key set, types) so downstream log scrapers do not break on shim updates.
close_reason: Added A2UI splitter metrics callbacks, structured per-turn metrics logging, parse/validation warning logs, verbosity toggle, and schema tests.

title: A2UI Phase 1: verify Anthropic prompt-cache usage on live model
description: Phase 1 implementation embeds the SDK-generated A2UI v0.9 Basic Catalog schema prompt and gates it behind WS capability negotiation. The admin-shim mock harness cannot prove Anthropic prompt-cache behavior because it does not call a live model. Run a live A2UI-enabled turn against Anthropic/Max Proxy, inspect usage reporting for cached_input_tokens/cache write behavior across repeated turns in one session, and document whether additional cache_control handling is needed.
acceptance_criteria: Live A2UI-enabled turn records usage from Anthropic/Max Proxy; repeated turn shows expected prompt-cache behavior or a follow-up implementation issue is filed with exact missing cache_control requirements; result is linked from lcp-uo5.2 notes.
notes: Local A2UI shim work is built/restarted and mock tests pass. This bead still requires a live Anthropic/Max Proxy run; current restarted shim is configured with LMSTUDIO_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8082/v1, so prompt-cache behavior cannot be proven from the mock/local harness.

title: Phase 3: Server-side A2UI schema validation + error handling
description:
## Goal

Validate every A2UI message emitted by the LLM against the v0.9 JSON Schema **before** forwarding to the client, so renderer never sees malformed input. Decide and implement the error-handling policy for invalid messages.

## Background

May 16 demo: 3/3 messages were schema-valid on first try. Production reality: this will not always hold. Reasoning models will sometimes produce invalid A2UI (wrong prop, missing required field, references to non-existent component ID). The shim is the right place to catch this — adding a server-side guard means the renderer can trust its input.

The Python SDK provides `a2ui.schema.validator.A2uiValidator` which takes a catalog and validates an A2UI message list (or single message) with optional `strict_integrity` flag (checks component references resolve).

## Tasks

- [ ] Wire `A2uiValidator` into the splitter from Phase 2
- [ ] Validate each A2UI frame as it's emitted from the splitter
- [ ] Decide error policy:
  - **Option A:** Drop invalid frames silently (log only)
  - **Option B:** Drop invalid frames + emit a synthetic `Text` fallback so the user sees *something*
  - **Option C:** Surface validation error to the agent on the next turn as feedback ("Your last A2UI emission was invalid because...")
  - Recommend: **C for development, A for production with metrics**
- [ ] Add metrics: `a2ui_validation_failures_total` counter, by failure type (schema vs integrity vs unknown)
- [ ] Add an opt-in debug mode that emits validation error details back to the agent's next-turn context for self-correction
- [ ] Test: feed deliberately-malformed A2UI through the validator and confirm graceful handling

## Acceptance criteria

- 100% of A2UI frames reaching the client are schema-valid
- Invalid frames produce a log line + metric increment, never crash the shim
- Debug mode: agent sees its validation failures on next turn (for testing/iteration)
- Integration test: malformed A2UI from a stub LLM is filtered cleanly

## Risks

- Strict integrity checks may reject valid streaming-partial states (component referencing a child that hasn't been emitted yet — but parent-before-child ordering should prevent this)
- Validator performance: don't want to slow down streaming. Validate per-frame, not per-byte.

## Dependencies

- Phase 2 (splitter must exist to validate output of)

## Reported by

Meridian + Emmanuel

title: WS turn_done.status=failed: bundle error code+message onto the frame (atomic-fail contract)
description:
Follow-up to lcp-axv. Currently failure emits TWO frames: error{code, message, ...} then turn_done{status:failed}. Wire order is correct (two consecutive safeSend calls on same socket; ws lib serializes), but the Android agent observed turn_done's handler running BEFORE the error's buffer-handler completed — a mobile-side coroutine race that drops the error message and falls back to 'Turn failed' generic UI.

Make the failure atomic-by-frame: extend turn_done with optional error_code and error_message fields (both null on non-failed turns). Mobile reads these when status=failed and skips the separate error-frame ingest path.

Wire shape after this lands:
  turn_done {
    turn_id,
    run_id,
    status: 'failed',
    lossy,
    drop_count,
    error_code: 'internal_error',
    error_message: 'pool spawn timeout for conv=default'
  }

The standalone error frame stays emitted before turn_done for forward-compat with existing consumers (and for non-terminal errors like cancel.run_not_found that don't close a turn). Mobile may keep buffering it but the turn_done's own fields are now authoritative for terminal failures.

Acceptance:
- ws-handler.mjs catch path: pass code + message into the turn_done frame.
- Test asserts both fields on turn_done(failed); error frame still emitted first; status=completed turns have null error_code / error_message.
- Mobile bead filed for the dispatcher update (read error fields from turn_done when status=failed).
- Update MOBILE_WS_STREAMING_CONTRACT.md Failure paths section to make turn_done's error fields the authoritative source.

title: lcp-nwd: pin LegacyLocalMessageWire shape with an exact-keys drift test
description:
**Why this matters**

`lcp-nwd` added a `run_id: string | null` field to the `LegacyLocalMessageWire` interface emitted by `localMessageToLettaMessage`. Adding fields is usually backwards-compatible, but the existing shim has no contract-pinning test that locks the exact shape of `LegacyLocalMessageWire`. If a mobile client or another consumer hardcodes the wire shape (an exhaustive type narrowing, a JSON schema validator, etc.), a silently-added field can still break it — and far worse, a *removed* field in a future change would silently break consumers with no test to flag it.

The cost of a contract-pinning test is small and the future-proofing payoff is large, especially under an autonomous loop where Ralph might add or rename wire fields based on a plausibly-described bead.

**Current behavior**

`LegacyLocalMessageWire` shape is defined only by its TypeScript interface in `admin-shim/lib/translate.ts`. No test asserts the full set of keys present in the emitted JSON.

**Desired behavior**

A test in `admin-shim/test/translate.test.ts` (creating it if absent) that:

1. Builds a representative `LocalMessage` (user/assistant/tool variants).
2. Calls `localMessageToLettaMessage` with a known scope.
3. Asserts the returned object has *exactly* the expected set of keys — no more, no fewer.
4. Repeats for a representative tool-call message.

The point is not the values; it's the **key set**. A drift test, not a behavior test.

Simultaneously, do a one-time `git grep` for `LegacyLocalMessageWire` and document any consumers — internal or in `home/.letta/channels/mobile/` — in the test file's comment block, so future readers know who depends on the shape.

**Non-goals**

- Adding strict-schema runtime validation (overkill).
- Changing the wire shape (this bead locks it as-is, including the new `run_id` field).
- Generating schemas from types (interesting, but separate concern).

**Rollback signal**

If the wire-shape test becomes a constant maintenance burden because legitimate wire-shape evolution requires touching it for every PR, revert and rethink — maybe a snapshot test instead of an exact-keys assertion. But default to keeping it strict; the whole point is to make changes visible.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `admin-shim/test/translate.test.ts` contains a test asserting that the keys of `localMessageToLettaMessage`'s output exactly match a documented expected set (no more, no fewer).
2. The expected key set includes `run_id` (from `lcp-nwd`) alongside all pre-existing keys.
3. A second test covers the tool-call message variant.
4. The test file documents — in a comment block — all known consumers of `LegacyLocalMessageWire` found via `git grep`.
5. Test fails when a new field is added or removed from the wire interface without also updating the test, proving it captures drift.

title: lcp-nwd: add gate locking 'oldest-run wins' merge semantics in buildMessageRunMap
description:
**Why this matters**

`lcp-nwd` introduced `buildMessageRunMap`, whose merge rule for the case where two runs claim the same `messageId` in their `message_ids[]` is **oldest-run-wins**. The docblock will (after `lcp-nwd-docfix`) state this explicitly, but there is no test pinning the behavior. Observable behavior without a gate drifts; this bead closes that drift surface.

The case is rare in practice (it would imply two runs both claimed the same persisted message), but the resolution rule is meaningful: it determines which run shows up in the mobile run-grouping UI when there's a conflict. A regression that flipped to newest-wins would silently move messages from one collapsible run-block to another with no test to flag it.

This bead is also a deliberate exercise of the "every new bead should add a gate, not just code" discipline from the autonomous-loop strategy discussion. The gate is the deliverable.

**Current behavior**

`buildMessageRunMap` implements oldest-run-wins (asc-ordered iteration + skip-if-set). No test covers the multi-run-claims-same-message case.

**Desired behavior**

A test in `admin-shim/test/runs.test.ts` (or a focused `translate.test.ts` if more appropriate) that:

1. Seeds two runs, A and B, where A was created earlier than B.
2. Both runs' `message_ids[]` include the same `messageId` `M`.
3. Calls `buildMessageRunMap({ agentId, conversationId })`.
4. Asserts the returned map has `M → A.id`, not `M → B.id`.

A second negative-direction test seeding the runs in reversed creation order should still resolve to the older run.

**Non-goals**

- Changing the merge rule itself.
- Adding a new public API to query attribution conflicts (out of scope; would be its own bead).
- Performance/memoization concerns (separate `lcp-nwd` follow-up).

**Rollback signal**

If the test as written turns out to be flaky against the existing seeding helpers (race on `created_at` resolution), revert and re-spec — do not weaken the assertion.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A new test is added that seeds two runs (oldest first), both claiming the same messageId, and asserts `buildMessageRunMap` returns the older run's id.
2. A companion test seeds the same configuration in reverse insertion order and still asserts older-run-wins (proves order-of-insertion does not affect merge resolution; only created_at does).
3. Tests fail when run against a buggy implementation that uses `out[mid] = r.id` unconditionally (newest-wins) — verified by temporarily breaking the code locally.
4. Tests pass on master after `lcp-nwd` lands.
5. No production code changes; `git diff --stat` shows only test files modified.

title: lcp-nwd: fix buildMessageRunMap docblock (says 'last writer wins' but code is 'oldest-run wins')
description:
**Why this matters**

The `buildMessageRunMap` function added in the `lcp-nwd` change set has a docblock that is internally inconsistent with the code below it. The text says "the LAST writer wins" and "listRuns returns desc-by-created-at" — but the code calls `listRuns({ order: "asc" })` and uses `if (!out[mid]) out[mid] = r.id`, which is **first-writer-wins on ascending-ordered runs**, i.e. **the oldest run that claimed a given messageId wins**.

The actual behavior (oldest run wins) is probably correct — the run that first attributed a persisted message should keep it — but the comment will mislead the next reader and is exactly the kind of "buried wrong context" that compounds in autonomous loops, because it's plausible-sounding wrong documentation that an implementing agent might trust over re-reading the code.

**Current behavior**

`admin-shim/lib/runs.ts::buildMessageRunMap` has an incorrect docblock describing its merge semantics. Code is correct; comment lies.

**Desired behavior**

Fix the docblock to state plainly:

> "We iterate `listRuns(..., order: 'asc')` — oldest-first — and use `if (!out[mid]) out[mid] = r.id`, so the **oldest run that claimed a given messageId wins**. This matches the intuition that once a run has attributed a persisted message, later runs cannot steal that attribution."

Remove the "LAST writer wins" and "desc-by-created-at" sentences entirely.

**Non-goals**

- Changing the actual merge semantics (the code is correct).
- Memoization or caching (separate concern, tracked in `lcp-nwd`-2 follow-up).

**Rollback signal**

None — docblock-only change.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `admin-shim/lib/runs.ts::buildMessageRunMap` docblock no longer contains the phrase "LAST writer wins" or "desc-by-created-at".
2. Docblock explicitly states that runs are walked in asc-by-created-at order and that the oldest claiming run wins.
3. `git diff --stat` confirms only `admin-shim/lib/runs.ts` is modified; no behavior change.
4. Existing `runs.test.ts` suite still passes unchanged.

title: Mobile WS: implement send_message content_parts for image attachments
description:
Shim side landed (commit forthcoming) — adds optional content_parts field to send_message frames, parsed in ws-handler.mjs, threaded through bridgeSendMessage → runTurn → worker stdin. When present, wins over the plain text field. Wire shape is Anthropic-style, identical to REST MessageCreate.content:

  {
    'type': 'send_message',
    'v': 1,
    ...,
    'text': 'Look at this',                   // fallback when content_parts absent
    'content_parts': [

title: Spec: define tool_output_chunk frame in MOBILE_WS_STREAMING_CONTRACT.md (predecessor to lcp-7wz)
description:
**Why this matters**

`lcp-7wz` proposes streaming `tool_output_chunk` frames over the mobile WS so long-running tool invocations render progressively instead of appearing frozen. Before that implementation work begins, the frame schema itself needs to be specified in the mobile WS contract document. Specifying the schema first means the client renderer, the server emitter, and the gate writers can all proceed against the same source of truth without ambiguity, and Ralph (or any other implementing agent) has a fixed target to code against rather than a fuzzy idea.

This bead is intentionally scoped to **specification only** — no code in `admin-shim/` or `home/.letta/channels/mobile/` is modified. The reward is a reviewable contract diff that's small, focused, and easy to argue about before any implementation lands.

**Current behavior**

`admin-shim/docs/MOBILE_WS_STREAMING_CONTRACT.md` defines the frame types currently emitted (assistant_message, reasoning_message, stop_reason, usage_statistics, tool_call, tool_result, etc.). There is no specification for incremental tool output — `tool_result` is the only tool-output-bearing frame, and it is emitted atomically on process exit.

**Desired behavior**

Add a new section to the contract document specifying `tool_output_chunk`:

- **Frame name:** `tool_output_chunk`
- **Required fields:** `tool_call_id`, `chunk_index` (monotonic, starts at 0), `stream` (one of `stdout` | `stderr`), `data` (string, may be empty).
- **Optional fields:** `is_final_chunk` (boolean; if true, no more chunks for this `tool_call_id` will be emitted before `tool_result`).
- **Ordering guarantee:** chunks for a given `tool_call_id` arrive in monotonically increasing `chunk_index` order over a single WS connection. Across reconnects, the client may receive replays or gaps — see reconnect semantics.
- **Reconnect semantics:** on reconnect, the server MAY replay missed chunks since the last acknowledged `chunk_index`, OR emit a `tool_output_replay_marker` frame indicating which chunks were skipped. (Pick one and document it; do not leave both as legal — that's exactly the ambiguity this bead is meant to close.)
- **Relationship to `tool_result`:** `tool_result` remains the terminal frame for every tool call. It is emitted after the last `tool_output_chunk` (if any) and carries final exit code, aggregate metadata, and may optionally include the full assembled output for clients that did not receive chunks.
- **Backwards compatibility:** clients that do not understand `tool_output_chunk` MUST be able to ignore it and still render correctly from `tool_result` alone. This implies servers MUST continue to emit a `tool_result` with full payload for tools that complete in <100ms (no chunking) and SHOULD emit a `tool_result` with full assembled payload even when chunks were sent (so the contract degrades gracefully).

Include a worked example showing the frame sequence for a `for i in 1 2 3; do echo $i; sleep 1; done` call: `tool_call` → `tool_output_chunk(0, stdout, "1\n")` → `tool_output_chunk(1, stdout, "2\n")` → `tool_output_chunk(2, stdout, "3\n", is_final_chunk=true)` → `tool_result(exit=0, output="1\n2\n3\n")`.

**Non-goals**

- Implementing the emitter or the client renderer (that is `lcp-7wz`).
- Specifying cancellation frames (separate future bead).
- Specifying chunk schemas for non-Bash tools (Read, Write, Grep, etc.) — those land later if/when each gets streaming support.

**Rollback signal**

If the schema review surfaces a fundamental ambiguity (e.g. the reconnect semantics chosen here conflict with how existing frame types handle replay), revert the contract change and re-spec rather than letting `lcp-7wz` ship against a half-defined contract.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `admin-shim/docs/MOBILE_WS_STREAMING_CONTRACT.md` gains a new section titled "tool_output_chunk" specifying the frame name, required fields, optional fields, ordering guarantee, reconnect semantics, and relationship to tool_result.
2. The section includes a worked example showing the exact frame sequence for a multi-line streaming Bash invocation.
3. Reconnect semantics resolve to a single chosen behavior (either server-replay OR replay-marker), not both as legal alternatives.
4. Backwards compatibility is explicit: clients ignoring tool_output_chunk frames still render correctly via tool_result alone.
5. No code is modified outside the contract document. `git diff --stat` against master shows changes only to `admin-shim/docs/MOBILE_WS_STREAMING_CONTRACT.md`.
6. `lcp-7wz` is updated to reference this bead as a dependency (blocked-by).

title: Stream long-running tool output progressively over mobile WS (line/time-buffered tool_output_chunk frames)
description:
**Why this matters**

Today, `tool_result` frames are emitted only when the subprocess exits. Any tool taking >1s (builds, tests, deploys, log tails, long greps) appears frozen on the mobile client until completion. From a UX perspective this is indistinguishable from a hang, and there is no signal anything is actually happening. Reconnect mid-execution loses the partial output entirely.

**Current behavior**

- `Bash` tool captures stdout + stderr in full, returns a single result frame on process exit.
- Mobile client renders the tool card as "running" with no body, then jumps to fully-populated on completion.
- Reconnect mid-execution drops any partial output.

**Desired behavior**

- Tool produces a stream of `tool_output_chunk` frames during execution, carrying delta stdout/stderr (line-buffered or time-buffered, whichever is cheaper).
- Terminal `tool_result` frame still emitted on process exit with final exit code and aggregate metadata.
- Mobile renders chunks progressively into the tool card body.
- Reconnect mid-execution can resume from the last seen chunk via a monotonic chunk index.

**Non-goals**

- Token-level streaming of structured tool output (JSON results, etc.) — line-level is enough.
- Cancellation UX — separate bead, but the chunked transport unblocks it.
- Retroactive change to non-Bash tools — scope this bead to Bash first; other tools follow.

**Rollback signal**

If mobile clients start dropping or duplicating tool output (visible in the user-facing tool card), revert and fall back to atomic frames.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Fixture: a Bash tool call running `for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do echo $i; sleep 1; done` produces >=5 distinct WS frames before the final `tool_result`.
2. The assembled chunk bodies, in order, byte-equal the final aggregate stdout.
3. A reconnect after frame 3 sees frames 4 and 5 (or a replay marker) — not silent loss.
4. The existing atomic-result path remains the contract for tools that complete in <100ms (no regression on fast calls).
5. Contract change documented in `admin-shim/docs/MOBILE_WS_STREAMING_CONTRACT.md`.

title: WS: confirm disconnect-mid-turn behavior; run record finalize must survive WS loss
description:
From contract review: mobile assumes 'disconnect mid-turn = lost; reconcile from disk' (no resume cursor, Phase 1). Shim must ALSO behave this way:
- When the WS closes mid-turn, the worker pool keeps running the turn
- onFrame writes to a dead socket — drops are expected

Action:
- Audit agent-pool.ts to confirm finalizeRun runs unconditionally on turn completion, even if the bridgeSendMessage onFrame closure has been thrown into a closed socket
- Add a test: ws: client disconnects mid-turn → server-side run record still transitions to status:'completed'
- Update MOBILE_WS_STREAMING_CONTRACT.md cancel/disconnect section: 'The shim does NOT resume; the run finalizes to disk regardless of WS state. Mobile reconciles from the run record on reconnect.'

title: WS: spec tool_call_message frame stream as progressive arg-accumulation (locked)
description:
From contract review: upstream letta-code emits tool_call frames as arguments accumulate (multiple frames sharing the same tool_call_id, with progressively more populated arguments). Mobile's existing newScore >= oldScore policy merges them correctly today. Spec needs a NORMATIVE statement so mobile keeps that policy, instead of treating it as inherited-from-SSE dead weight.

Action:
- Add to MOBILE_WS_STREAMING_CONTRACT.md: 'tool_call_message MAY arrive multiple times for the same tool_call_id during a turn; each frame represents the arguments known at emit time. Consumers MUST merge by tool_call_id with last-wins-when-more-complete semantics.'

- Verify the upstream frame's id is forwarded verbatim so mobile sees the same toolcall-<id> across frames (already in lcp-cv3 ws-handler change).

title: conversation.last_message_at and updated_at never bumped after creation
description:
agent-pool.ts calls stampNewMessages after every turn, which correctly updates the per-message _real-times.json sidecar. But conversation.json's last_message_at and updated_at are written exactly once in server.ts:505 at create time and never touched again.

Effect on mobile:
- Mobile sorts the conversations list by last_message_at (GET /v1/conversations?order_by=last_message_at)
- All values are stuck at conv creation time, which for migrated convs is the migrator default (2026-01-01)
- Real recent activity in _real-times.json (current values around 2026-05-15T14:21Z) is invisible to the list sort
- 'Last activity' / relative-time strings rendered on conversation rows are all wrong

Concrete evidence (default conv):
  _real-times.json max = 2026-05-15T14:21:21.473Z
  conversation.json.last_message_at = 2026-01-01T00:07:57.000Z

Proposed fix:
- stampNewMessages tracks the max ISO it stamped this turn and patches conversation.json's last_message_at/updated_at atomically when it's larger than the existing value
- One-shot backfill: walk migrator/out/conversations/*/conversation.json, set last_message_at/updated_at = max(current, max(_real-times.json values))

title: WS stop_reason envelope uses 'reason' field; REST/SSE/Kotlin model use 'stop_reason'
description:
The WS handler wraps the stop_reason frame with a `reason:` field
(home/.letta/channels/mobile/lib/ws-handler.mjs:~234-239), but every
other surface uses `stop_reason:`:

  REST / SSE / Run record:  { "stop_reason": "end_turn" }
  Kotlin Message.kt `StopReason`:  @SerialName("stop_reason") val stopReason
  letta-code raw stream frame:     { "stop_reason": "end_turn" }

Only the WS path emits:

  { "type": "stop_reason", "reason": "end_turn", ... }

Impact for the new mobile ChannelTransport (letta-mobile-9vgk):
  - Kotlin clients cannot reuse the existing StopReason.serializer()
    directly on the WS path — they need a separate WS-stop-reason
    DTO that maps `reason` to the same stopReason field.
  - Confusing for anyone debugging the protocol with mixed traffic.

Verified by running:
  grep "reason" home/.letta/channels/mobile/lib/ws-handler.mjs | head
  grep "stop_reason" admin-shim/lib/chat.ts | head

Fix:
  - Rename the WS envelope field `reason` -> `stop_reason` in
    ws-handler.mjs.
  - Update the WS test that checks for the `reason` field
    (ws-protocol.test.ts: "ws: stop_reason frame carries reason field").
  - Update MOBILE_WS_PROTOCOL.md section 2.2 + 4.7 to drop the
    divergence note.
  - The mobile ChannelTransport implementation will then use the
    canonical StopReason model directly.

This is a contract change observable to any existing WS client. There
are none in production yet (the new mobile WS pipeline is unbuilt) so
the cost is low; do it before letta-mobile-9vgk ships.

Filed during Mobile WS doc drafting.

@see admin-shim/docs/MOBILE_WS_PROTOCOL.md section 2.2 stop_reason + 4.7
@see home/.letta/channels/mobile/lib/ws-handler.mjs:~234-239
@see letta-mobile/.../data/model/Message.kt StopReason
@see admin-shim/lib/chat.ts (REST/SSE emit shape for comparison)

title: Missing GET /v1/tools/{tool_id} — mobile tool-detail screen 404s
description:
Mobile's ToolApi.getTool(toolId) calls GET /v1/tools/{tool_id} and
expects a single Tool record back (see letta-mobile ToolApi.kt:34).

server.mjs:847 only routes:
  - GET /v1/tools          → handleTools (list)
  - GET /v1/tools/count    → BUILTIN_TOOL_DEFINITIONS.length

There is no by-id handler, so detail requests fall through to the
catch-all and 404. Mobile's tool-detail screen breaks.

Fix:
  - Add a regex match: /^\/v1\/tools\/(tool-[^/]+)\/?$/ on GET.
  - Look up the id against BUILTIN_TOOL_DEFINITIONS.map(vanillaTool).
  - Return the matching record (200) or 404 with a Letta-style error
    body.
  - Add a behavioral test in admin-shim/test/http-contract.test.mjs:
    happy path + unknown-id 404.

Use the deterministic id formula already in server.mjs:336 —
`tool-${base64url("tool:" + name).slice(0,24).toLowerCase()}` — so the
list and detail records share the same id for the same name.

Note: vanilla Letta also supports lookup by name on this route, but
mobile only ever calls by id (per the Ktor client). Stick to id-lookup
unless mobile starts using name.

title: bug: getMobileChannelAdapter races on concurrent first call
description: mobile-channel-host.mjs:157 memoizes cachedAdapter only after plugin.createAdapter() and adapter.start() complete. If two WS upgrades arrive during cold start, both pass the cachedAdapter null-check, both import the plugin, both call createAdapter, and both call adapter.start(). Result: two adapters live, one orphaned, potentially two account sessions.
design: Cache the in-flight Promise rather than the resolved value: let cachedAdapterPromise = null; on first call set it to (async () => { ... })(); subsequent calls await the same promise. On rejection, clear it so a retry is possible.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent first-callers all receive the same single adapter instance; start() runs exactly once.
notes:
TS migration update (2026-05-15, post-phase-7c): file renamed mobile-channel-host.mjs → mobile-channel-host.ts. Updated locations:
- mobile-channel-host.ts:290 — cachedAdapter module-level variable
- mobile-channel-host.ts:297 — getMobileChannelAdapter() definition
- mobile-channel-host.ts:300 — the racy null-check
- mobile-channel-host.ts:332 — the late cache assignment
Strict-mode is on, so the recommended fix (cache the Promise, not the resolved value) needs a proper Promise<MobileChannelAdapter | null> type. The .d.ts published in lcp-dab means external channel plugin authors will start exercising this path — race likelihood goes UP, not down. Worth prioritizing.

title: perf: synchronous fs in request path blocks event loop
description: store.mjs uses readFileSync / writeFileSync / readdirSync / statSync throughout, and these functions are called from inside the async WS and REST handlers via bridgeSendMessage and friends. For small JSON files the cost is negligible, but slurping a long messages.jsonl with readFileSync blocks the Node event loop, hurting concurrent client latency.
design: Audit all store.mjs exports for which are called from request-path code. Convert listMessages, stampNewMessages, the sidecar writers to async first. Keep listAgents/listConversations* sync only if behind the caching from the related bead — otherwise async those too.
acceptance_criteria: Hot-path filesystem operations on potentially-large files (messages.jsonl, sidecars) use fs/promises. Small one-off reads of accounts.json/conversation.json may stay sync if simpler.
notes: TS migration update (2026-05-15, post-phase-7c): all referenced files renamed .mjs → .ts. The sync fs pattern survived the migration — readFileSync/writeFileSync/readdirSync/statSync are still used throughout store.ts. With node:fs/promises now available and strict-mode on, converting to async is mostly a mechanical change but will ripple into agent-pool.ts and mobile-channel-host.ts callers (they'll need to await). Recommend doing this AFTER lcp-y88 and lcp-ayo land — those changes reshape what gets called on the hot path.

title: perf: listAgents / listAllConversations have no caching
description: store.mjs:54 listAgents and store.mjs:101 listAllConversations both do unconditional directory walks + JSON.parse per file. If any REST handler hits these per-request (likely candidates: conversation list, agent list, the resolveConversationId fallback path) the cost compounds.
design: Add a thin module-level cache keyed on (root path, root mtime). On call, statSync the root dir — if mtime matches the cached entry, return cached; otherwise rebuild. Acceptable staleness for these is on the order of seconds; mtime check is single syscall vs full walk.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated calls within a short window do not re-walk the filesystem. Cache invalidates correctly when underlying files change.
notes:
TS migration update (2026-05-15, post-phase-7c): files renamed .mjs → .ts. Updated locations:
- store.ts:194 — listAgents() (was store.mjs:54)
- store.ts:256 — listAllConversations() (was store.mjs:101)
With strict-mode on, the cache values are now typed (OnDiskAgentRecord[], OnDiskConversation[]) — easier to wrap with a typed memoizer.

title: perf: assistant_message coalescing rebuilds growing string per chunk
description: mobile-channel-host.mjs:107-119 coalesces streamed assistant_message chunks by concatenating reshaped.content onto pendingAssistant.content (string += string). For very long replies this allocates a new growing string per chunk. Also pendingAssistant = { ...reshaped } shallow-clones the frame on first arrival.
design: Buffer chunks as an array of strings on pendingAssistant.parts and only join at flushPendingAssistant() time. Avoid the spread by retaining the first reshaped object and mutating it; we already own it post-reshapeFrame().
acceptance_criteria: Memory pressure during long streamed replies is bounded; string assembly is amortized rather than O(n²) in chunk count.
notes:
TS migration update (2026-05-15, post-phase-7c): files renamed .mjs → .ts AND coalescing partially extracted. Updated locations:
- mobile-channel-host.ts:141 — pendingAssistant declaration (BridgeFrame typed)
- mobile-channel-host.ts:183-187 — string-concat hot path
- chat.ts:386 — coalesceAssistantFrames() now exists as a separate exported function
Important: the SSE path now uses coalesceAssistantFrames() in chat.ts:620; the WS path in mobile-channel-host.ts still has its own inline state machine. Fix should be done in BOTH (or by unifying onto a shared createAssistantCoalescer helper — see lcp-05c which is now half-done).

title: admin-shim: document/expose headless-test-client contract surface on /shim/v1/mobile
description:
The admin-shim /shim/v1/mobile WS is the canonical live transport for mobile (and soon desktop). Today the only consumer that drives it as a 'real client' is the Android app — humans only, manual repro. Curl probes hit shim but don't act as a real client (no Timeline reducer, no RuntimeEvent outbox, no projection).

letta-mobile is filing a companion ticket (letta-mobile-q9t4t) to graduate its :cli module into a headless test client that consumes the SAME WS contract the Android app does. For that to work cleanly:

1. The mobile WS protocol contract surface should be documented as a public-facing test target — not just an internal mobile<->shim convention.
   - welcome frame structure (already in admin-shim/docs/MOBILE_WS_PROTOCOL.md §12)
   - canonical_live_transport + transport_contract block (landed 2026-05-25)
   - per-run seq + run_id stamping (lcp-pro just landed)
   - send/receive frame schemas
   - reconnect/resume cursor semantics

2. Confirm nothing in /shim/v1/mobile assumes 'this caller is an Android client.' If there's any UA-sniffing, device-id assumption, or notification-routing coupling, expose it as opt-in headers rather than implicit behavior.

3. Optional: a small shim-side ws-probe helper script (or graduate ws-probe.mjs currently in working tree) that documents the minimal hello -> welcome -> send -> receive loop a headless client must implement.

Scope: small. This is a documentation + audit task, not a new feature. The actual headless client lives in letta-mobile, not here.

Why P3: not blocking anything; nice-to-have once letta-mobile's :cli graduates. If letta-mobile :cli ends up being the de-facto canonical headless client (which is the right outcome), this ticket may close as 'covered by the documentation that ships with that work.'

Reference:
- letta-mobile-q9t4t — companion ticket in letta-mobile rig
- admin-shim/docs/MOBILE_WS_PROTOCOL.md §12
- admin-shim/ws-probe.mjs (untracked, working tree)
acceptance_criteria:
1. MOBILE_WS_PROTOCOL.md has a 'Headless clients' section pointing at the contract surfaces a non-Android client must implement.
2. Audit confirmed: no implicit Android-only assumptions in /shim/v1/mobile path. Any client-type-specific behavior is opt-in via headers or capability negotiation.
3. ws-probe.mjs either graduated to a documented diagnostic helper or removed.
4. letta-mobile :cli (or any future headless client) can connect to /shim/v1/mobile without shim modifications.

title: TimelineRepository not session-scoped — stale timeline loops survive backend switch
description: TimelineRepository is a @Singleton with an internal LinkedHashMap<String, TimelineSyncLoop> keyed by conversation ID. Stale loops survive backend switch — they point to the old backend's conversation IDs. Evicted by LRU cap but no explicit flush on session change. Fix: subscribe to session changes and clear the loop cache on switch, or make TimelineRepository session-scoped.

title: Per-agent collection jobs in SessionScopedPassageRepository leak on navigation
description: SessionScopedPassageRepository.getPassages() creates a permanent launchIn(proxyScope) coroutine per agentId (line 42-53). Never cancelled even when the agent screen is dismissed. Each job collects via flatMapLatest forever. Fix: tie job lifecycle to the collecting scope, or use reference counting to cancel jobs when no collectors remain.

title: MobileWsHandle.waitFor short-circuits on existing frames, breaks multi-turn collectTurn
description: admin-shim/test/helpers/ws.ts: waitFor() returns instantly if any prior frame in conn.frames matches the target type. collectTurn() uses waitFor under the hood, so a second sequential turn on the same socket sees turn 1's stale turn_done and returns an empty slice. Worked around in admin-shim/test/sdk-conversation-stability.test.ts with a local collectNextTurn(cursorBefore) helper. If more multi-turn tests appear, lift collectNextTurn into helpers/ws.ts as a handle method (or change collectTurn's contract to take a cursor).

title: Doc: A2UI theme.primaryColor regex is strict 6-digit hex — theme_hints must match before forwarding
description:
Per the embedded basic_catalog.json (a2ui-v09-basic-prompt.ts), theme.primaryColor is constrained to ^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$ — strict 6-digit hex, no 3-digit shorthand ('#FFF'), no rgba(), no named colors.

If mobile's hello frame theme_hints ever carries a non-matching value, and we wire theme_hints into the prompt (per lcp-vup), the model will be told to copy it into theme.primaryColor, and the renderer's catalog-schema validator will reject the resulting surface.

This pairs with lcp-vup (theme_hints injection). When implementing that fix:

1. Pre-validate primaryColor on the shim side before forwarding into the prompt. Drop or normalize invalid hex shapes.
2. Document the constraint in admin-shim/docs/MOBILE_WS_PROTOCOL.md §2.1 hello.theme_hints — note primaryColor regex, and that color_scheme ('light'|'dark'|'system') is a free-form hint that does NOT map directly into theme.primaryColor.
3. Add a one-line server log when theme_hints fails pre-validation, so mobile-side regressions surface quickly.

Pure documentation + a defensive pre-validation step. Low priority but cheap to land alongside lcp-vup.
close_reason: Documented theme_hints.primaryColor strict 6-digit hex constraint and implemented/logged pre-validation before prompt forwarding.

title: Doc: A2UI Action has two shapes — server event (round-trips via user_action) vs client functionCall (local-only)
description:
A2UI v0.9 common_types.json defines Action as a oneOf between:

1. Server-side event: { event: { name: string, context: object } }. Triggers a server-side handler. In our transport, the mobile renderer dispatches this as a user_action WS frame. Round-trips to the agent.

2. Client-side functionCall: { functionCall: { call: string, args: object, returnType: ... } }. Executes locally on the renderer (e.g. openUrl, formatDate inside a Button context). Does NOT round-trip to the server.

Currently undocumented in admin-shim/docs/MOBILE_WS_PROTOCOL.md §2.1 user_action section. If a mobile developer naively wires every Button.action onto the WS path, openUrl-style actions will be sent over the wire and dropped — the shim has no handler for client-side function call shapes, and the agent would not know what to do with them anyway.

Fix: add a one-sentence note to MOBILE_WS_PROTOCOL §2.1 user_action: 'Only Action shapes carrying an event field map to user_action frames. functionCall actions are local — handle them in the renderer without WS round-trip.'

Purely a doc fix. Mobile-side concern but worth tracking on our side so the protocol doc stays authoritative.
close_reason: Documented that only A2UI Action.event maps to mobile user_action frames; functionCall remains renderer-local with no WS round-trip.

title: A2UI: validateA2uiMessage 'ok' flag means envelope-valid, not render-valid — rename or document
description:
The splitter's A2uiBlock.ok field (admin-shim/lib/a2ui-stream-splitter.ts:39, 177) means 'parse + envelope-validation passed', NOT 'the renderer will accept this'.

Things validateA2uiMessage intentionally does NOT enforce (per its doc comment, lines 183-197 — 'deeper component-tree validation lives in the renderer'):
- A component with id='root' exists in updateComponents.components (spec REQUIRES this — see embedded schema description).
- Component IDs referenced by Card.child / Row.children / Tabs.tabs[].child actually exist.
- Per-component required props: Button needs action+child, TextField needs label, Slider needs max, ChoicePicker needs options+value, etc.
- catalogId on createSurface matches the negotiated capability (see lcp-2wb).

This is the right trade-off — a streaming envelope-only splitter shouldn't try to model surface state. But downstream code (and the WS frame consumer) sees ok:true and may assume more than the validator delivers.

Fix options:

(a) Rename ok → envelopeValid. Cascade to the WS frame contract (a2ui_frame.ok → a2ui_frame.envelope_valid). Loudest fix; requires mobile contract update.

(b) Add a docstring on A2uiBlock.ok clarifying scope, and add the same note in MOBILE_WS_PROTOCOL §2.2's a2ui_frame description.

Recommendation: (b). Cheaper, conveys the meaning without breaking the wire contract.
close_reason: Clarified a2ui_frame.ok/A2uiBlock.ok as parse plus structural envelope-valid, not renderer/catalog-valid.

title: Doc: A2UI version-string asymmetry — handshake uses '0.9', JSON envelope uses 'v0.9'
description:
The shim uses two different version-string formats:

- Handshake field a2ui_version on hello/welcome/capabilities frames: '0.9' (no v prefix). Defined in a2ui-adapter.ts:3 DEFAULT_A2UI_VERSION = '0.9'.
- JSON envelope version field inside emitted A2UI messages: 'v0.9' (with v prefix). Enforced by validateA2uiMessage at a2ui-stream-splitter.ts:210 and required by the embedded schema's {const: 'v0.9'}.

Both are technically correct relative to upstream: the handshake is our invention, the envelope is per-spec. But the asymmetry is a footgun for anyone reading just one file.

Fix: document prominently in admin-shim/docs/MOBILE_WS_PROTOCOL.md §2.1 (hello) and §2.2 (a2ui_frame). Add a short note in admin-shim/lib/a2ui-adapter.ts above DEFAULT_A2UI_VERSION explaining the two-format split.

No code change required if we keep the asymmetry. Alternative: normalize to 'v0.9' for the handshake too, before mobile ships. Coordinate with mobile-side work.
close_reason: Documented handshake/capability version "0.9" vs A2UI envelope version "v0.9" in protocol docs and adapter comments.

title: lcp-nwd: per-request memo + observable cap-hit warning for buildMessageRunMap
description:
**Why this matters**

`lcp-nwd`'s `buildMessageRunMap` walks up to 10,000 runs per call. It is invoked once per call to `handleAgentMessages`, once per call to `handleAgentContext`, and once per call to `handleConversationMessagesList`. For active conversations with many runs, this is repeated work that scales with conversation history rather than with the request.

Two real concerns:

1. **Silent cap.** The `limit: 10_000` is generous but finite. A long-lived agent that crosses 10k runs will silently drop the oldest runs from attribution — messages claimed by those older runs will lose their `run_id` projection and start rendering ungrouped on mobile. The user-visible symptom would be "old chat blocks suddenly become flat" and would be very hard to attribute back here.

2. **Hot-path cost.** No memoization across requests, and within `handleAgentContext` the function is built once and threaded through, which is fine — but `handleAgentMessages` and the conversation/run-messages paths each build their own. For a chat-screen poll burst (mobile fetches messages + agent context + runs around the same moment), that's 3× the work.

**Current behavior**

`buildMessageRunMap` is called inline per handler with no memoization, with an implicit 10k-run cap that emits no warning when reached.

**Desired behavior**

Pick one or both (smaller bead can implement just one):

1. **Per-request memo.** Cache `buildMessageRunMap({agentId, conversationId})` results in a `WeakMap`-keyed-by-request, or pass a single computed map into the handler chain that needs it. Eliminates the double-call within a single request lifecycle.

2. **Cap-hit observability.** When `listRuns` returns exactly 10,000 results (the cap), emit a structured warning log with `agentId`, `conversationId`, and a one-line "attribution-incomplete: increase cap or paginate" note. Optional: a counter exposed via the existing metrics path. This converts a silent-incorrectness bug into a loud-incorrectness bug.

A more ambitious version would memoize across requests in a TTL'd LRU keyed by `(agentId, conversationId, last_run_created_at)`, but that's a separate scope and likely premature optimization until 1+2 are in place.

**Non-goals**

- Removing the 10k cap entirely (that's a separate decision; the cap exists for a reason).
- Cross-process caching (Redis, etc.) — over-engineered for the actual hot path.
- Changing the merge semantics (covered by `lcp-nwd` and its docfix follow-up).

**Rollback signal**

If memoization introduces a stale-attribution bug where a new run's `message_ids[]` is added but a cached map still shows the message attributed to no run / a different run, revert the memo and fall back to per-handler builds. The cap-warning piece has no rollback risk.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Either (a) `buildMessageRunMap` is invoked at most once per request lifecycle in handlers that need it, OR (b) a clear comment explains why per-handler invocation is necessary.
2. When `listRuns` returns exactly the configured cap (10,000), the shim emits a structured warning containing agentId, conversationId, and a remediation hint.
3. A test exercises the cap-hit path by stubbing `listRuns` to return the cap and asserts the warning is emitted.
4. A test exercises the no-memo-stale path: a new run is inserted between two handler calls and the second handler sees the updated attribution.
5. No regression in existing `runs.test.ts` suite.

title: WS cancel.run_id: spec says required, server falls back to currentRunId
description:
The mobile WS protocol documentation (admin-shim/docs/MOBILE_WS_PROTOCOL.md,
sections 2.1 and 4.5) treats `run_id` as required on `cancel` frames.
The defending test name reads as a strict contract:

  ws-protocol.test.ts: "ws: cancel with no run_id and no active turn ->
  error{protocol_violation}"

But the actual server-side handler is lenient:

  home/.letta/channels/mobile/lib/ws-handler.mjs:~291
    const runId = frame.run_id ?? currentRunId;
    if (!runId) return sendError("protocol_violation", ...);

A `cancel` frame with no `run_id` is accepted IF there's a current
in-flight turn — the server uses `currentRunId` as the implicit target.
The protocol_violation only fires when neither is available.

Disagreement: the doc and test name say "must carry run_id", the code
says "run_id OR current in-flight turn". Both are reasonable; only one
is the contract.

Fix options:
  A. Tighten the server to require run_id on every cancel — gives a
     cleaner spec, but slightly less ergonomic for clients that have
     a UI-level "cancel current turn" button and don't track run_ids.
  B. Loosen the doc + test name to allow the implicit fallback —
     matches today's runtime, but the new mobile ChannelTransport
     (letta-mobile-9vgk) would have to handle either path.

Recommend (A) — explicit cancels are more debuggable. The mobile bead
already documents the explicit-run_id pattern as the contract; tightening
the server keeps the surface honest.

Filed during Phase 4c (lcp-7sf) audit / Mobile WS doc drafting.

@see admin-shim/docs/MOBILE_WS_PROTOCOL.md section 4.5
@see home/.letta/channels/mobile/lib/ws-handler.mjs:~291
@see admin-shim/test/ws-protocol.test.ts (the cancel-with-no-run_id test)

title: translate.mjs tool-return emits scalar stdout/stderr where mobile expects List<String>
description:
translate.mjs (now translate.ts) tool-return branch passes through
`part.stdout ?? null` and `part.stderr ?? null`, which can be a bare
scalar string when the upstream LocalMessage carries one. Mobile's
Kotlin Message.kt:237-238 declares these as `List<String>?`, so a bare
string at runtime would fail kotlinx.serialization decoding.

In practice this path is "rare" — most tool-return paths emit
`stdout: null, stderr: null` (the auto-approved native tool branch in
translate.ts:515-516 and 534-535). The scalar passthrough only fires
when the LocalMessage part carries a non-null scalar, which appears to
be uncommon enough that no captured fixture or test exercises it.

The wire types in lib/types/wire.ts have been widened to
`string | string[] | null` for ToolReturn.stdout/stderr and
ToolReturnMessage.stdout/stderr to preserve the existing runtime
behavior. The fix is to wrap scalars into a single-element array at
the emit site, but that's a behavior change and was deferred per the
TS-migration epic's "no behavior changes" rule (see lcp-dxa).

Discovered during Phase 3c (lcp-u3q). The Phase 3c agent attempted to
fix it inline; reverted on parent review.

Fix plan:
  - Before changing the emit, prove the scalar path can actually fire
    (write a fixture / disk file that has scalar stdout, observe the
    wire output).
  - Then wrap scalars into a single-element array in the tool-return
    branch.
  - Tighten the wire types back to `string[] | null`.
  - Add a regression test that captures the array-wrapping behavior.

@see lib/translate.ts:551-552, 575-576

title: runs.ts:292 only sets background:false, never true
description:
runs.mjs:108 hard-codes Run.background=false on creation. The wire
type defines `background?: boolean` and RunsListParams.background is
honored as a filter on the way in — but creation never sets it true.

title: refactor: bridgeSendMessage assumes vanilla framing for all channels
description: bridgeSendMessage in mobile-channel-host.mjs unconditionally reshapes via reshapeFrame and runs the assistant_message coalescing logic. This matches mobile/vanilla's 'one assistant_message per turn' contract, but if a future channel (or a different mobile build) wants raw chunks for incremental rendering, the coalescing is baked in.
design: Move the coalescing state machine into a small composable helper (createAssistantCoalescer({ onFrame })). bridgeSendMessage takes options { reshape: true, coalesce: true } and composes. Each channel plugin can declare its desired framing in accounts.json or its createAdapter() return.
acceptance_criteria: Channels can opt into or out of coalescing without forking bridgeSendMessage. Reshape vs. raw is also configurable per channel.
notes:
## Premise outdated — closing as wontfix (2026-05-19)

The original premise — "extract a shared createAssistantCoalescer helper used by both bridgeSendMessage and chat.ts" — no longer matches reality.

Since lcp-cv3 landed, the WS path in mobile-channel-host.ts:200+ deliberately does NOT coalesce assistant_message frames. The comment block at line 202 locks the contract:

> "lcp-cv3: stream assistant_message and reasoning_message chunks as they arrive — DO NOT coalesce server-side. Mobile's stream ingest (TimelineSyncIngest.kt) expects PURE DELTAS per the lettabot-uww.11 contract."

Mobile renders incremental chunks with a 60fps reveal loop in StreamingDisplayTextSmoother.kt. Server-side coalescing would re-introduce first-chunk latency without UX win.

The SSE/REST path in chat.ts:386 retains `coalesceAssistantFrames()` because the REST contract returns ONE assistant_message per turn (vanilla shape). These are two intentionally-different framing models, not a duplication.

A reusable coalescer would still be a nice abstraction in theory, but with only ONE caller (chat.ts), the abstraction has no second consumer to justify it. If a future non-mobile channel arrives that wants vanilla-style coalescing, that's the right moment to extract — not before.

No code change. Closing as wontfix; lcp-cv3's contract supersedes this bead's design.
close_reason: premise superseded by lcp-cv3; WS path now explicitly non-coalescing — no shared helper needed

title: perf: readOtidMap re-reads file immediately after writing it
description: After writeOtidForLocalId in bridgeSendMessage, the next findUnmappedTailUserMessageId call (on the very next turn) re-reads the same sidecar via readOtidMap. The file is small but every turn pays a syscall + parse the previous turn already paid.
design: Module-level Map keyed by  holding the in-memory otid map. writeOtidForLocalId updates the map and the disk file; readOtidMap returns the map if present, otherwise loads from disk into the map. Largely subsumed by the JSONL-sidecar rework but useful as a cheap intermediate step.
acceptance_criteria: Otid map for an active conversation is held in memory and updated in-place on write; disk read happens only on cold load.

title: chat.mjs SSE pendingStop/pendingUsage are last-wins, not first-wins
description:
chat.mjs (now chat.ts) buffers pendingStop and pendingUsage during the
SSE stream and flushes them once at the tail via flushTail. If upstream
emits multiple stop_reason or usage_statistics frames in a single turn,
the LAST one survives — not the first.

This works in current fixtures because the last-arriving frame happens
to match the expectation, and the "exactly once on the wire" tests
("stop_reason emitted exactly once even when the trace has multiple",
"usage_statistics emitted exactly once even with multi-step traces")
pass.

The end-to-end "FIRST frame wins" contract documented in HANDOFF.md is
enforced separately: agent-pool's collector pushes the FIRST usage and
stop_reason to runs.ts finalizeRun. So:
  - Run-level usage / stop_reason (on the Run record): FIRST ✓
  - SSE-stream-emitted usage / stop_reason frames: LAST

Worth tightening to first-wins so the contracts agree end-to-end. Watch
this if a multi-step turn's SSE frames ever look "wrong" — e.g. the
stream's stop_reason says "end_turn" but the run says "requires_approval".

Filed by Phase 4b (lcp-ry1) audit.

title: TS migration tightened disk-shape input validation vs .mjs (audit findings)
description:
The Phase 3a (runs.ts) and Phase 3b (store.ts) conversions added type
guards (isRunRecord, isStep, isLocalMessage, isAgentRecordCandidate,
isConversationOnDisk, isStringRecord) that reject malformed disk
records the original .mjs would have forwarded. Read-only audit
findings:

runs.ts (commit 563baab):
  - listRuns/aggregateUsage filter coercion: r.agent_id ?? "",
    r.status ?? "". Only diverges if a caller passes literal null in
    the agentIds/statuses array — never happens via HTTP.
  - aggregateUsage model group-by: empty/non-string s.model collapses
    to "unknown" instead of being its own key. No real step record
    has s.model = "".
  - recordRunStep id: typeof === "string" instead of nullish. Caller
    paths always pass string or undefined.
  - getRun/listRuns/aggregateUsage/listRunSteps: shape guards skip
    records missing a string id; mjs would have read them as-is.
  - cancelRun/deleteRun: err.message via instanceof Error coercion
    (logging only).

store.ts (commit e789f4a):
  - listAgents / getAgentRecord: isAgentRecordCandidate requires
    non-empty string id. mjs accepted numeric/truthy ids.
  - listConversationsForAgent / listAllConversations / getConversation:
    isConversationOnDisk requires both id and agent_id strings; mjs
    only did truthy checks.
  - listMessages: isLocalMessage requires id:string, role:string,
    parts:Array. Real on-disk JSONL always has these. If letta-code
    evolves the schema and drops parts, new code silently skips;
    mjs would have forwarded then crashed downstream.
  - readMessageTimestamps / readOtidMap / writeOtidForLocalId:
    isStringRecord rejects sidecars with any non-string values.
    Sidecars are shim-written; impossible in practice.
  - _internals is now Object.freeze'd. Only consumer is read-only.

Verdict: all findings are pathological-input-only against current
real-world data (sampled state/ and migrator/out/ — every row passes
the new guards). Net effect: silent no-op for malformed records
instead of downstream crash — arguably more robust.

This bead exists as documentation, not a fix target. If a future
schema change in letta-code's LocalBackend writes a row that misses
e.g. `parts`, this is where to look first.
notes:
## Audit closure (2026-05-19)

This bead is a read-only audit log of where Phase 3a/3b's .mjs→.ts conversion tightened disk-shape validation (added isRunRecord / isStep / isLocalMessage / isAgentRecordCandidate / isConversationOnDisk / isStringRecord type guards).

Per the original audit:
- All tightening cases require malformed records that the original .mjs would have forwarded as-is. In practice no real on-disk JSONL row triggers them (the migrator writes well-formed records).
- The guards CORRECTLY reject hand-crafted corruption. The new behavior is "skip silently" vs "crash later" — that's a hardening, not a regression.
- The audit identifies no behavioral break against the production migrator output.

No acceptance criteria were attached because no code change was proposed. The audit's value was recording the divergence points for future reference, which the issue body already does in detail.

Closing as completed — the tightening is intentional, the audit is filed in the issue body, no fix is needed unless a real corrupted record shows up in production (in which case the row's source — not the validator — is the bug).
close_reason: audit closed — TS tightening is intentional; no behavioral break observed against migrator output
